item.title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Charlie Keller
item.author: Jonathan Farrar
item.content:encoded: Before he was a star for the Yankees, Charlie Keller was a small-town boy on a Maryland farm. In a truly poetic life journey, that is exactly the life that he would return to after playing 13 years in the major leagues, with a gap year in there to serve as a merchant marine. September 12, 1916 (Middletown, MD) May 23, 1990 (Frederick, MD) 1939-1943, 1945-1949, 1952Keller came of age working on the family farm and eventually became a standout athlete at Middletown High School, just a bit outside Frederick, Maryland. While at Middletown, Keller was a state champion in track while playing baseball, basketball, and soccer. With the book smarts to match his athletic ability, Keller went to the University of Maryland on scholarship. While in undergrad, Keller played both basketball and baseball at the varsity level, gradually turning into one of the greatest Terps to ever grace the diamond.Baseball became the sport that the right-hand-throwing and lefty-swinging Keller would come to dominate. After an impressive showing both in school and during a semi-professional league, Yankees scout Gene McCann signed Keller to a contract just before the start of the 1937 season.At 20 years old, Keller’s professional journey officially began as a member of the Newark Bears. Upon reporting to spring training, the Yankees informed Keller they planned to play him in right field, a new position. The Yankees also spent the 1937 season trying to get the stout lefty to focus on pulling the baseball. In his first taste of pro ball, Keller slashed .353/.431/.541 with 13 home runs, 14 triples, and 34 doubles. Keller ditched the pull approach ahead of the 1938 season and went on to win the batting title with a .353 average while also leading the league in runs and hits. For his efforts, he was named both the International League Rookie of the Year and Minor League Player of the Year of 1938.Skipper Joe McCarthy and the Yankees gave Keller his first taste of pro ball in 1939. After missing the start of the season due to injury, the rookie, who was now primarily playing left field, finally made his debut at the end of April. The rookie struggled to find playing time over the first few months of the summer, but starting in August, the kid caught fire and would force his way into the lineup through the end of the regular season and into the Fall Classic.New York swept the Cincinnati Reds in the 1939 World Series as Keller had a team-high .438 average, to go along with three home runs and six RBIs. The rookie’s triple in the ninth inning of Game 1 (as seen below) led to a walk-off hit by Bill Dickey and set the tone for the series. In the Game 4 clincher, he came around to score in the 10th inning on a chaotic play started by a Joe DiMaggio hit. An E9 enabled Keller to come home, and as he did so, he collided with Reds catcher Ernie Lombardi. The dazed Lombardi was slow to come to his senses and by the time he’d done so, DiMaggio had scored himself. The sweep was completed shortly afterward.The 1940 season was the start of a legendary run for Keller. He was an All-Star in 1940, leading the league in base on balls while batting .286 with 21 home runs. The Yankees would miss the playoffs that season after finishing 88-66 and third in the American League.Keller had one of, if not his best, seasons in 1941. He hit .298 and posted career highs in home runs with 33 big flies and 122 RBIs. Keller finished fifth in the MVP vote and was an All-Star for the second time. The Yankees found themselves back in the World Series and Keller impressed again, batting .389 while driving in five runs and scoring another five himself. In the most memorable highlight from that series, Yankees batter Tommy Henrich Brooklyn catcher Mickey Owen both missed a wicked pitch from Hugh Casey, and what would have been a strikeout for the end of a series-tying Dodgers win in Game 4 instead continued with Henrich on first. DiMaggio singled and Keller became the one to really twist the screws with a two-run double that put the Yankees ahead, 5-4.Both the Yankees and Keller had a bit of a disappointing year, for their standards, in 1942. Keller posted a .292/.417/.513 slash line behind 26 home runs and a career-high 14 stolen bases. The Yankees made the World Series but lost to the Cardinals 4-1; Keller was held to four hits in five games, though two were homers.The 1943 campaign saw Keller get his third All-Star selection as he led the league in base on balls again and OPS with a .922 and OPS+ of 168. The Yankees again found themselves facing the red bird of St. Louis in the World Series. This time, the Yankees prevailed in five games, giving Keller his third ring in five seasons.Then, in January of 1944, everything changed for Keller as he was commissioned into the U.S. Maritime Service. Keller would serve in the Pacific for the next 20 months. In August of 1945, Keller returned to the Yankees for the final stretch of the season. Despite still having his sea legs under him, Keller hit .301 with 10 home runs in 44 games as the Yankees finished third in the league.The 1946 Yankees also finished in third place and missed the playoffs, but Keller returned to his pre-war form and was again an All-Star. On the season, Keller launched 30 home runs, driving in 101, and drawing 113 base on balls to give him his fifth career season to exceed 100+ walks.Keller was still in top form for the first third of the 1947 season. Entering June, he was leading the league in several offensive categories and would earn his fifth All-Star selection in just a few weeks. Little did anyone know, but a small tweak of his back while taking a swing forever changed his career. Keller ended up having surgery to remove a slipped disk in July. Keller missed the rest of the season and had to watch from the dugout as his teammates took down the Dodgers in seven games to win the 1947 World Series.The legendary swing from King Kong Keller was never the same. Despite trying to work his way back into form, Keller struggled in 1948 and 1949. Over those two campaigns, he slashed .262/.378/.405 with only 9 home runs in 143 games. The man once a lock for 600 at-bats and 100 walks was no more. In another bittersweet moment, Keller watched his teammates win the 1949 World Series.As a Yankee, Keller finished his career with a slash line of .286/.410/.518 with an OPS of .928 and a WAR of 42.3 in 1066 games. His .410 career OBP ranks him top 5 all-time in Yankees franchise history. Keller also averaged roughly three walks for every two strikeouts, which is crazy for a slugger like him.The Tigers signed Keller after the Yankees released him in 1949. Keller spent the 1950 and 1951 seasons mostly appearing as a pinch-hitter for the Tigers. In limited action over those two years, Keller hit .283 with five home runs. The Yankees brought Keller home for the 1952 season. However, after only one at-bat in 1952, the Yankees released Keller and his playing career was over.After his playing days ended, Keller returned to Maryland and started Yankeeland Farm. He remained on the farm for the remainder of his days except for when the Yankees asked him to don the pinstripes again as a coach during the 1957 season. Keller stuck with the team under Casey Stengel through the end of the 1959 season. While he served as the team’s first base coach, the team lost the 1957 World Series but get revenge and win the 1958 World Series in a rematch with the Milwaukee Braves. That ring gave Keller his sixth as a Yankee.Though it was cut short, Keller’s peak was one remarkable run. Three modern players who can help put his career into perspective, according to Baseball Reference’s Similar Batters, are Juan Soto, Josh Hamilton, and Cody Bellinger. Another comparison is Bryce Harper as the athletic, converted catcher, super-slugging lefty. In an organization with some of the greatest of all time, Keller might truly be the greatest what-if in pinstripe history.See more of the “Yankees Birthday of the Day” series here.

item.title: Marquez outfoxes Bezzecchi to take crucial Misano sprint win
item.author: Valentin Khorounzhiy
item.content:encoded: Defending MotoGP champion Marc Marquez defeated title rival Marco Bezzecchi to win the sprint race at Misano.Equipped with the medium rear tyre - versus the conventional sprint choice of soft - Marquez pounced on Bezzecchi immediately at the start, using a marginally better getaway to take control of the inside line into Turn 1.He had far too much pace early on for Bezzecchi, building a lead of over a second - though Bezzecchi did whittle this down to around the 0.5-0.6s mark in the second half of the 13-lap race.But the fastest lap of the race from Marquez on lap 11 broke his resistance, and he settled into second behind Marquez.Points leader Jorge Martin mitigated the damage by completing the podium - which means he now heads Marquez by 14 points and Bezzecchi by 22.Fifth after the start, Martin quickly picked off Fermin Aldeguer and then later in the race overtook outside title contender Fabio Di Giannantonio - pouncing at Turn 6 and then fighting off the Ducati on the straight out of the corner.Di Giannantonio and Alex Marquez completed the top five, the latter having made the most of an Aldeguer v. Pedro Acosta battle up ahead of him to clear both.That battle ended up putting Aldeguer in the firing line of Raul Fernandez, too, and he ultimately came home behind both Acosta and Fernandez, and ahead of last points-scorer Luca Marini.Fabio Quartararo was the only rider to crash, falling off when he ran out of room trying to squeeze past Diogo Moreira on the inside. He remounted to finish 21st and last.1 Marc Marquez (Ducati)2 Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia) +1.068s3 Jorge Martin (Aprilia) +3.538s4 Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Ducati) +3.968s5 Alex Marquez (Gresini Ducati) +4.348s6 Pedro Acosta (KTM) +6.944s7 Raul Fernandez (Trackhouse Aprilia) +7.707s8 Fermin Aldeguer (Gresini Ducati) +8.832s9 Luca Marini (Honda) +11.712s10 Johann Zarco (LCR Honda) +14.534s11 Dario Morbidelli (VR46 Ducati) +17.043s12 Franco Morbidelli (VR46 Ducati) +17.405s13 Francesco Bagnaia (Ducati) +17.763s14 Brad Binder (KTM) +18.181s15 Enea Bastianini (Tech3 KTM) +18.476s16 Pol Espargaro (Tech3 KTM) +18.752s17 Jack Miller (Pramac Yamaha) +21.113s18 Toprak Razgatlioglu (Pramac Yamaha) +20.698s*19 Alex Rins (Yamaha) +21.740s20 Joan Mir (Honda) +22.054s21 Fabio Quartararo (Yamaha) +24.419sRazgatlioglu received a one-place penalty for track limits on the last lap

item.title: Calls for Democrats to be shot go unchallenged at Republican convention

item.content:encoded: Crowd member repeatedly said some Democrats ‘should be shot’ during Ted Cruz’s speech, without senator respondingOn the night Republicans gathered to mourn the killing of Charlie Kirk and warn against the dangers of violent rhetoric, a crowd at the party’s irregular midterm convention in Dallas repeatedly called for a sitting Senate candidate to be shot, while the Republican senator at the podium never denounced or even noted the outbursts.The outbursts came repeatedly during Ted Cruz’s Thursday night address at the American Airlines center, when he named a Democrat he accused of holding radical views. After the senator mentioned the New York City mayor, Zohran Mamdani, video footage depicts at least one audience member shouting: “He should be shot!” The same cry followed when Cruz named Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, and again after he named Texas Senate candidate James Talarico. Cruz did not pause or respond to the shouting, and it remains unclear whether he heard it from the stage. Cruz did not respond to a request for comment.Continue reading...

item.title: Yankees Rivalry Roundup: Rays walk off Astros in series opener
item.author: Madison Pavich
item.content:encoded: The Yankees kicked off the Subway Series with a win, scoring six on the Mets and managing to hold on despite the anomaly that was Paul Blackburn and Brent Headrick both struggling on the same night. David Bednar came in for the five-out save and got the job done, escaping a bases-loaded jam in the eighth before getting a game-ending double-play out of Juan Soto in the ninth. While they were handling business in the Bronx, they were also scoreboard watching with several key games going on simultaneously — so let’s see what the result of those out of town scores were.Tampa Bay Rays (88-59) 3, Houston Astros (75-73) 1The Rays looked like they could’ve slipped up and lost this game ceding some ground to New York, but they came around to walk it off instead. Houston had their chances against Drew Rasmussen, scattering eight hits against the Rays’ ace, but the only run they managed to score came in the fourth inning when Isaac Paredes doubled with one out and Daulton Varsho singled to put runners on the corners. Yainer Diaz hit a ball hard to second base, and while Ritchie Palacios made a fantastic play on the ball flipping it to the shortstop quickly enough for the force out keeping the potential double play alive, Diaz managed to beat the throw letting the run count. However, several other innings were cut short by double plays that did get converted, and the Rays tied the game back up in the fifth when Victor Mesa Jr. launched a home run to lead off the inning.Things stayed quiet until the bottom of the ninth, when the Rays got the winning run aboard on an Aranda double before Junior Caminero stepped up to the plate. Bryan Abreu chose to start him off with a fastball up in the zone and Caminero made him pay, ripping a walk-off two-run shot to left.The win not only kept the Rays three games ahead of the Yankees in the standings, but it clinched a playoff spot for Tampa Bay — the first team to secure a spot in the 2026 Postseason. The Brewers would join them a little later in the night with a blowout win on their part, but the Rays are, for now, the only American League team holding a ticket to the dance.Boston Red Sox (80-68) 2, Kansas City Royals (66-82) 3: The Yankees did gain some ground on Friday, as the Red Sox fell behind early to Kansas City and couldn’t dig themselves out of the hole. Carter Jensen led off the game against Sonny Gray with a double and later scored on a Salvador Perez single to left, and then the Royals added to their lead in the third as Isaac Collins and Jensen hit back-to-back doubles followed by a Vinnie Pasquantino RBI single. Mickey Gasper got Boston on the scoreboard in the fifth with a solo shot, and after Adley Rutschman walked Wilyer Abreu doubled him in to cut the lead to 3-2. The Sox struck out from there though, and Boston would get just one hit the rest of the way stranding a Trevor Story double in the eighth.Chicago White Sox (75-72) 3, St. Louis Cardinals (73-75) 7: The White Sox are squandering their advantage in the Central, losing their fourth straight game. The Cardinals scored a run in each of the first three innings, but they delivered the knockout punch in the fifth as Jordan Walker, Alec Burleson, Joshua Báez, and Leo Bernal chained consecutive hits to drive in three runs. The Cardinal bullpen dealt with some traffic on the basepaths but managed to limit Chicago to just one run in the final 4.2 innings. Chase Meidroth showed up for the Southsiders, launching two home runs to briefly keep them within arm’s reach of St. Louis.Cleveland Guardians (75-73) 5, Minnesota Twins (69-78) 2: Chicago’s faltering opens the door for Cleveland, who moved to within a half-game of first place after taking this one against the Twins. The game was tied at two in the ninth when a wild pitch and a two-run double from Brayan Rocchio put them up three in a heartbeat. Cade Smith entered looking for the save and got the job done quickly with a double-play ball to erase a one-out single from Trevor Larnach.Toronto Blue Jays (73-75) 4, Baltimore Orioles (72-76) 7: The O’s jumped out to a 6-0 lead in this game, scoring five in the second inning with two-run hits from Colton Cowser and Dylan Beavers leading the procession. Toronto had a rally in them in the ninth, scoring two runs on a Brett Bateman homer before George Springer and Vladimir Guerrero Jr. hit singles to bring the tying run to the plate. Unfortunately for Toronto this all came with two outs, and when Baltimore went back to their ‘pen summoning Rico Garcia to pitch he managed to get Alejandro Kirk to ground out to end it.Texas Rangers (72-76) 1, Arizona Diamondbacks (79-69) 9: Two innings were all Arizona needed to put up a nine-spot on Texas in a rematch of the 2023 World Series. A trio of doubles in the fifth led to four runs scoring for the Diamondbacks, followed by Corbin Carroll and Nolan Arenado launching back-to-back homers in the sixth to drive the dagger home. Justin Martinez had the highlight of the night for the pitching staff, tossing an immaculate inning in the top of the sixth shutting the door on any potential response from Texas after Arizona took the lead.

item.title: Hamilton, Bearman crash in final Madrid F1 practice
item.author: Jack Cozens
item.content:encoded: Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli headed a final Spanish Grand Prix practice session at the Madring featuring two red flags, including one for a Lewis Hamilton crash at the final corner.Antonelli ended up 0.166s clear of Hamilton's Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc, the long-time pacesetter before the first red flag and after the session resumed, with the McLarens of Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris improving to third and fourth in that period too.But Hamilton's crash was the session's most noteworthy moment - even if Ollie Bearman's late red-flag inducing crash was the biggest of the Madring weekend yet.Hamilton had just set the fastest middle sector of all (which still stood as the fastest at the end of the session) when he crashed at the final corner 23 minutes into FP3, locking up and heading nose-first, square-on into the Tecpro barrier.He found reverse gear from there and, despite protestations from Ferrari to stop the car, attempted to limp his SF-26 back to the pits.With the front wing rubbing against the front-right tyre, which became punctured, Hamilton did eventually park the Ferrari at Turn 14 - though only after he was told by race engineer Carlo Santi: "It's a formal request, they [the FIA] told us to stop in the safest place possible. Stop before Turn 12 [La Monumental], on the left."Repairs to the barrier took a significant amount of time, which prompted race control to take the unusual step of pausing the clock to prevent the session time from elapsing before track activity could continue on what is only the second day of official F1 running at the track.FP3 did finally resume 39 minutes after the red flag was shown with a quarter of an hour left on the clock, a period in which Leclerc improved his best time before Antonelli set the fastest lap of the weekend so far, a 1m32.797s.Any further changes to the head of the order were prevented by Bearman's crash, which came at Turn 10, the first part of a right-left leading into the circuit's banked La Monumental corner.Bearman did not appear to clip the wall but lost the car at the apex and spun, which pitched his car backwards into the barrier on the outside of the subsequent left-hand bend.He was assured by his Haas team afterwards not to worry and that the team would "get it rebuilt" before qualifying, but significant damage to the left-hand side of his car suggested that is far from guaranteed.Max Verstappen completed just seven laps in the session but ended up fifth-fastest in the best of the Red Bulls, two places but more than seven tenths faster than team-mate Liam Lawson. George Russell was sandwiched between them in the second of the Mercedes cars.Hamilton's time was still good enough for ninth, with the Audis of Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto either side of him.Alex Albon was the only driver not to set a time. He glanced the barrier with the left-hand side of his car exiting the penultimate corner and could not rejoin the session, even after the long pause in proceedings.1 Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) 1m32.797s2 Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) +0.166s3 Oscar Piastri (McLaren) +0.189s4 Lando Norris (McLaren) +0.236s5 Max Verstappen (Red Bull Racing) +0.375s6 George Russell (Mercedes) +0.702s7 Liam Lawson (Red Bull Racing) +1.105s8 Nico Hulkenberg (Audi) +1.136s9 Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) +1.487s10 Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi) +1.491s11 Franco Colapinto (Alpine) +1.549s12 Esteban Ocon (Haas) +1.633s13 Oliver Bearman (Haas) +1.684s14 Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) +1.708s15 Yuki Tsunoda (Racing Bulls) +1.768s16 Pierre Gasly (Alpine) +2.174s17 Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin) +2.223s18 Carlos Sainz (Williams) +2.667s19 Lance Stroll (Aston Martin) +2.773s20 Sergio Perez (Cadillac) +3.644s21 Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac) +3.873s22 Alexander Albon (Williams) — no time

Deepfakes are wrecking influencers’ credibility, one fake ad at a time
item.author: Arielle Pardes
item.content:encoded: Influencers aren’t just battling competitors for brand deals. They’re now battling AI versions of themselvesEarlier this year, Emily Schuman, the creator of the lifestyle blog Cupcakes and Cashmere, saw a photo of herself she didn’t recognize on Instagram. In a sponsored ad, Schuman, who has more than 500,000 Instagram followers, is holding up a vial of GLP-1 drugs, advertising the telehealth company Gala. There was just one problem: Schuman had never heard of Gala and had nothing to do with the ad.The ad was based on a digitally altered version of a selfie Schuman had taken in her car and posted on Instagram years earlier. Once her followers got wind, they flooded her inbox with questions about the sponsorship as it didn’t seem consistent with Schuman’s personal brand. Soon after, Schuman discovered this was just the beginning. There was also an Instagram post where an AI version of her with darker hair appears to apply foundation to promote a makeup brand called Meroda Cosmetics, and TikTok posts with generated images of her promoting the blood testing company Superpower.Continue reading...

item.title: 'The ambition is victory' – French teams announced for Montreal World Championships with Paul Seixas and Célia Gery taking leadership roles
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: The French squads for the Road World Championships in Montreal, Canada, have been announced, with Paul Seixas and Célia Gery leading the charge at the head of the men's and women's teams.19-year-old Seixas will take on the elite men's road race for the second time in his career after finishing 13th in Rwanda last year. The Frenchman, who took bronze in the UEC Road European Championships a week later, has enjoyed a stunning season, with standout results including wins at La Flèche Wallonne, Itzulia Basque Country, and fourth at the Tour de France."The ambition is victory," French coach Thomas Voeckler told . "I would have said the same thing even if Pogačar had been there, though I would have believed it a little less."We're not favourites, but we still have a rider who's not just any rider, one of those guys who can look any other rider straight in the eye."Seixas will be accompanied by two Decathlon CMA CGM teammates in the squad in the form of Nicolas Prodhomme and Jordan LabrosseValentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal-Quick Step), Pavel Sivakov (UAE Emirates-XRG), Alex Baudin (EF Education-EasyPost), Bruno Armirail (Visma-Lease a Bike) are also part of the lineup, while the participation of another Visma rider, Louis Barré, remains in doubt following a crash at the GP de Québec.The French women's lineup won't feature Pauline Ferrand-Prévot, who will "take the time to rest and recover for the remainder of the season" ahead of the 2027 campaign, her Visma-Lease a Bike team said."Contrary to what has been reported, Pauline is not disinterested in the French team; she remains motivated and proud to wear the jersey," national coach Paul Brousse told ."Her team had identified three key events in her season: the Ardennes Classics, the Tour de France, and possibly the European and World Championships at the end of the season. After the Tour, she and her team decided not to resume training and competition."Instead, 20-year-old Célia Gery will lead the way for France. She has impressed this season in supporting Demi Vollering to Giro and Tour victories as well as winning Brabantse Pijl and the French road title.She'll be joined in the team by FDJ United-SUEZ teammates Juliette Berthet, Marie Le Net, Léa Curinier and Evitz Muzic as well as Cédrine Kerbaol (EF Education-Oatly) and Maëva Squiban (UAE Team L'IMAD)."The plan is to play our cards right, to create favourable race moves," said Brousse."There won't be a single leader; we'll rely on our teamwork. Facing us is Demi Vollering, who is having an exceptional season and is really focused on the World Championships."The Dutch team will be a force to be reckoned with in the race, and we'll have to disrupt them with the help of teams like Belgium and Italy."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: We know how to prevent black lung, so why are workers still dying?
item.author: Sara Sneath
item.content:encoded: Silicosis sufferers are getting younger as Trump and the coal mining industry push back on protectionsSilicosis is one of the oldest workplace hazards and public health experts have known for decades how to prevent it. Yet a new wave of workers, from Appalachian coalminers to Latino countertop fabrication workers, are developing and dying from the disease as industry fights new protections and regulators fail to defend the rules that could protect them.John Robinson’s grandfather developed black lung back when coalminers could spend decades in the mines before being diagnosed with the disease, often dying in their 60s, 70s and 80s. But Robinson, who mined for coal in south-west Virginia, was diagnosed when he was 47. He’s part of a trend that has grown over the past two decades in central Appalachia, where more coalminers are developing black lung disease at younger ages.Continue reading...

item.title: Can Anthony Volpe’s changes help him take advantage of Yankees’ opportunity?
item.author: Andrés Chávez
item.content:encoded: To say that Anthony Volpe’s MLB career to this point has been a disappointment would be an understatement. He has certainly had his moments, but a first-round pick producing an 85 wRC+ in parts of four campaigns is definitely not what you want, 2023 Gold Glove notwithstanding. Having said that, it’s impossible to deny that the kid is a hard worker and seems determined to make it work at the highest level.After the Yankees promoted George Lombard Jr. immediately following the Trade Deadline, Volpe was sent to the minor leagues. He didn’t use the time to play around or publicly complain about fate and harsh roster decisions. No, he used it to train, work, and try to become the best version of himself he could be.Volpe made adjustments at the plate, increased his focus, and started to perform and put up numbers in Scranton. From August 7th to September 7th—exactly a month’s worth of stats—he hit .284/.381/.642 with a 1.023 OPS, a 159 wRC+, 10 home runs, seven doubles, and eight steals as well. Additionally, he worked in other infield positions other than shortstop, increasing his versatility by spending the bulk of his time at the keystone, plus a few games at the hot corner.Of course, Volpe has raked in the minor leagues before; that’s part of what excited Yankees fans about him in the first place, especially in 2022. The challenge will be doing it in the majors, but he got off to a solid start with a 3-for-4 performance on Thursday against the Rockies as a second baseman filling in for the injured Jazz Chisholm Jr. One of those hits was a grand slam to the Short Porch, and on the night, he drove in five while stealing a base.Nobody rational is losing their minds over one game, but there are some changes he implemented in his batting stance and timing mechanism that are worth discussing. A Twitter user named Victor posted a video comparing Volpe’s stance earlier in 2026 and one from Thursday’s game, and the difference is quite clear.The swing seems much more explosive. Obviously, being healthy after offseason labrum surgery helps, but the infielder seems to have incorporated a step-back move to fully load and then unleash his power on pitches. The swing path also looks different, in this lone example, at least. Well, for a day, at least, it all worked, but his Triple-A performance this past month can’t be completely ignored, either.Since they have a pressing need at second with Chisholm out and he only made three appearances at the hot corner in the minors, Volpe is expected to be used almost exclusively at the keystone in the short-term, although it’s nice to know he could be an emergency option across the infield if something comes up. All things considered, the former Gold Glover does have some exciting potential to help the Yankees in the next week or two. He just has to take advantage of his opportunity.Although it almost feels as though Volpe has been around forever, the man is still just 25 years old. Fate and his own hard work have given him a chance to put himself on the map again—especially as the Yankees enter an offseason where Chisholm may depart in free agency. It’s likely to be a brief window in terms of immediate 2026 impact, so he needs to show something.Whatever happens with Volpe when Chisholm returns is anyone’s guess, because the latter is expected to slide back to his starting role once he’s deemed healthy enough to play. For the former, however, it all starts with making a good impression in the handful of MLB games he will be given in the next couple weeks, and we aren’t talking exclusively about stats: how his swing looks, how he fares in adversity, how he looks with the glove, and his level of intensity and focus will all be evaluated. It’s one thing to have a big game with the cellar-dwelling Rockies in town; it’s quite another to do so against tougher foes, especially if he remains a factor for the Rays series from September 22-24 (though Chisholm could be back by then).Volpe has a brief but meaningful chance in front of him, regardless of whether or not it results in a spot on the postseason roster, or if there’s a potential impact on 2027 plans. Those are discussions for another time. The here and now is all that matters for Volpe.

item.title: Knicks face tough Miles McBride decision after latest contract-talks update
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: Miles “Deuce” McBride enters the 2026-27 season as the longest-tenured New York Knicks player following Mitchell Robinson’s exit and he’s surely turned into an important contributor for the reigning champs after averaging a career-high 12.0 points while shooting 41.3% from three last season.According to SNY’s Ian Begley, the Knicks and McBride’s representatives have remained in regular contact, but New York’s financial situation could make a long-term extension difficult.“This one is tricky because Miles McBride has definitely earned a raise,” Begley reported. “He’s outplayed his contract (3 years, $13 million) by a significant amount.”McBride is entering the final season of that contract. Begley noted Knicks owner James Dolan’s mandate not to exceed the NBA’s $221 million second apron this season as the major roadblock for reaching such an agreement.Potential extensions for Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart and eventually Jalen Brunson will inevitably increase the money committed to New York’s starting lineup, and McBride looks like the one set to absorb most of the collateral damage — assuming all parties find a way for him to stay.“So there isn’t much financial wiggle room for a McBride extension,” Begley reported.In a promising updated and despite the constraints, neither side has given up on the possibility of extending their relationship.“In a perfect world, those conversations would produce a multi-year extension for McBride,” Begley reported. “The longest-tenured Knick, McBride loves New York, loves his teammates; he was an integral part of this team’s rise.”We all know the alternative, as harsh and hard to stomach it might be: trading Deuce before next year’s deadline. That said, there’s no doubt McBride is one of (if not the absolute best) the lague’s most valuable sixth-man trade chips and would attract significant interest from other teams.“We’re certainly not there yet,” Begley reported. “But logic tells you that’s where things could be headed.”For now, McBride is set to enter the season with New York with one year left on his deal and a date we’ll all remember no matter what ends up happening circled in his calendar: ring night in late-October.

item.title: 'We will now be in the third or fourth row of favourites' – Slovenia announce squad for Road World Championships with Primož Roglič as leader in Tadej Pogačar's absence
item.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
item.content:encoded: Slovenia has announced its team for the upcoming Road World Championships in Canada, with Primož Roglič leading the men's selection in the absence of two-time world champion Tadej Pogačar.Roglič, currently battling for the red jersey in the final weekend of the Vuelta a España, will lead the Slovenian men's squad in Montreal, guiding an eight-man team in the road race.He'll be joined by Jan Tratnik, Matej Mohorič, Luka Mezgec, Matevž Govekar, Gal Glivar, and Tilen Finkšt, while Vuelta breakthrough rider Jakob Omrzel is the likely eighth man.The women's team will see Urška Zigart joined by Nika Bobnar in a two-rider squad. Bobnar and Tratnik will both take part in the time trial."It's true that we don't have Tadej in our ranks, which is a handicap, but also an advantage. We see that Primož is in a form he hasn't been in for a long time, and Jan is also in form," Slovenian national selector Uroš Murn told ."Let's hope that we will also get permission for Jakob to compete. All the attention that would have been on us will now be focused on the Belgians and the French. We will now be in the third or fourth row of favourites."Roglič has a mixed record at Road World Championships over the years, with a sixth place in Imola 2020 his best road race result. He took silver in the time trial at the 2017 Worlds in Bergen, Norway, meanwhile.Murn said that the hilly course in Montreal is suited to Roglič's abilities."Primož probably can't believe in himself yet and I believe he will be able to take advantage of that. The slopes in the race suit him, the route is technically not that demanding, as the roads are wide."It will be important to position him in the group to protect him at the front and to ensure that he has the help he needs."Now all the national teams' appetites have grown after they experienced the shock of Pogačar's withdrawal. Everything will change. For me, the favourite is Remco Evenepoel, but I think they will have friction within the team, because Wout van Aert, who is racing exceptionally in the Vuelta, also wants to win."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: As it happened: triumphant day for the Spanish on climactic stage 20 of the Vuelta a España
item.author: Stephen Puddicombe
item.content:encoded: For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go! Hello and welcome to stage 20 of the Vuelta a España - the queen stage of this year's race. September 12, 2026 – 6:15 AMEnric Mas might not have looked troubled throughout his whole time in the red jersey so far, but he hasn’t had to face anything like this all race. It’s a monstrous stage, with five mountains in total, three of them rated category one, and the last rated Hors category as the toughest of them all. It’s a hard enough stage to turn this Vuelta on its head, even at this late stage of the race. Anything could happen. September 12, 2026 – 6:22 AMYesterday didn’t quite produce fireworks in the GC race, with attacks not coming until the final few kilometres, and everyone in the top five finishing at the top of the summit finish together. But today there surely will be, given the severity of the parcours, and the fact this is the last chance at this Vuelta before the final circuit stage in Granada.September 12, 2026 – 6:29 AMToday features more climbing than any other stage of this race by some distance. But as one merciful relief for the riders comes in the temperature, which is cooler than it was earlier in the race, in the early twenties rather than the thirties.September 12, 2026 – 6:35 AMThe riders are in the neutralised zone, and will be racing the Queen Stage soon. The first 40km are about as flat as this stage gets, and even they take place on rolling terrain. It’ll be a massive fight to get into the break, and only riders still feeling (relatively) strong after three weeks of racing will be able to get into it. September 12, 2026 – 6:39 AMAnd they're off! And its Wout van Aert who is among the first to kick things off, going on the attack with UAE's Oliveira. The pair have a gap of about ten seconds over the peloton, where more are trying moves. September 12, 2026 – 6:45 AMAll of the attacks from behind Van Aert and Oliveira have been neutralised, but the leading duo press on.Does Van Aert have his eye on the King of the Mountains jersey? He's 38 points behind Santiago Buitrago after the Colombian's ride in the breakaway yesterday - but there are a total of 53 points to be won today.September 12, 2026 – 6:52 AMWhile the battle for the break continues, Carlos Rodríguez has had to drop back to his team car to get a radio issue sorted out. This isn't the kind of day you want to be without radio communication for, as it's likely to be very chaotic. That is indeed the case now, and multiple riders try to join Van Aert and Oliveira at the front of the race. September 12, 2026 – 6:56 AMAdding to the complications of the day, there's also a bit of wind on the exposed section the peloton is riding through, and a group of about a dozen riders have used it to help et a gap on the peloton. Uno-X Mobility were the chief instigators, putting three men in the group. September 12, 2026 – 6:59 AMThe wind has caused a split in the peloton - and Mas has been caught out! Multiple Movistar teammates have dropped back to help pace him, but it's unclear for now whether he is in the same split as his GC rivals, or if they are in the group ahead. September 12, 2026 – 7:03 AMMovistar have brought the front peloton back, which does appear it did contain Roglič. That's an early scare for Enric Mas, but one he has managed to see off.Up ahead, the chase group instigated by Uno-X have caught Van Aert and Oliveira, and lead the reunified peloton by 18 seconds. September 12, 2026 – 7:07 AMActually, the chase group had not caught Van Aert and Oliveira - they're only doing so now. Here was the pair right at the start of the day, when they broke clear of the peloton.September 12, 2026 – 7:12 AMUno-X Mobility have almost their entire roster in this breakaway, with six riders present, including their best climber Tobias Halland Johannessen. Cofidis also have two, as does Roglič's RedBull with Vermeersch and Fisher-Black. The Slovenian has satellite riders up the road, while Mas has none - he must be hatching a plan to make a move on the red jersey. September 12, 2026 – 7:16 AMAre Movistar panicking?Having set a pace for a few kilometres, they’ve now fired a couple of riders up the road, Garcia Pierna and Romeo, in an attempt to bridge up to the break. They must be feeling anxious at having nobody in the break especially as Roglič has a couple, but are also toeing up rival teammates Thornely (of Red Bull) and Shaw (of EF). But these are questionable tactics, and they could be burning off key domestiques very early. September 12, 2026 – 7:19 AMThe Movistar duo are still riding, and have picked up some riders between the peloton and the lead group on their way - including more EF and Red Bull teammates. They're committed to the move, and are desperate to make up the remaining 15 seconds they need to join the lead group. September 12, 2026 – 7:22 AMTwo riders have gone down in the peloton. Riccitello is one of them, and thankfully for his team leader Gall, he's back on white bike. But Hamilton looks hurt, and will likely abandon the race. September 12, 2026 – 7:28 AMHere's the group at the front, and there about to start climbing - up the first of five mountains on the menu today.They lead the peloton by about 40 seconds, with the chase group behind led by Movistar somewhere in between.September 12, 2026 – 7:34 AMThe ploy isn't working for Movistar, as the chase group led by Romeo and García Pierna (and EF, who are contributing now) are failing to make up ground on the leaders, being kept at 35 seconds. The worst case scenario for Movistar is if the pair working burn themselves out trying to chase, but fail to bridge up to the lead group, and are then too tired to assist Mas later in the stage, potentially leaving him isolated and very outnumbered by Red Bull.September 12, 2026 – 7:41 AMThe lead group crests the climb, with Buitrago's teammate Pau Miguel ensuring he takes the points ahead of Van Aert. Buitrago is in the chase group behind, so will, like the Movistar pair in it, want to bridge up to the leaders. As do EF, who have a few domestiques helping Movistar lead the pace. There's plenty of investment in this group, but they're almost a minute behind. September 12, 2026 – 7:46 AMThere are no threats to GC in either of the groups ahead of the peloton, but plenty of domestiques of the favourites who could help swing the balance of power.Roglič has two teammates in the lead group, and another two in the chase group; Mas has no teammates in the lead group, and two in the chase group; Gall one in the lead group and one in the chase group; Onley none in the lead group, two in the chase group; and finally Carapa has none in the lead group, but four in the chase group. September 12, 2026 – 7:52 AMWhile the peloton has sat up and are happy to let both the lead group and the chase group have a gap, the lead group has not, and does not want the 30-or-so riders in the chase group to join them. They're keeping the pace high, and increasing their lead, to over one and a half minutes. September 12, 2026 – 7:59 AMDespite initially getting up on his bike, Riccitello has abandoned the race following his crash. That's bad news for Gall, for whom he had become the main mountain domestique for, since Mühlberger's abandon earlier in the race. September 12, 2026 – 8:03 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 12, 2026 – 8:12 AMThe gaps between the groups are getting bigger and bigger. The lead group is now three minutes ahead of the chase group (which is actually about 50 riders big), meaning they are unlikely to come together. But the peloton is over five minutes behind the chase group; so Movistar do look like they're going to get what they wanted, which was not the stage win, but rather teammates far enough up the road to act as satellite riders for Mas. September 12, 2026 – 8:21 AMThe riders are climbing again, this time up the first category one of the day. It's the Puerto de El Purche, and averages a brutal 8% for 8.2km. The leaders have started it with a gap of 3:30 over the chasers and a huge ten minutes over the peloton. September 12, 2026 – 8:29 AMThis climb is starting to see the inferior climbers struggle, as Tiller and Vermeersch (one of Roglič's two teammates in the lead group) are dropped. Meanwhile in the chase group (pictured), Movistar are setting the pace again, with García Pierna, Romeo and Castrillo.September 12, 2026 – 8:35 AMThe peloton might be over eight minutes behind the chase group, but that hasn't stopped Sepp Kuss from attacking on the climb. Presumably his teammates up the road (of which there are four, plus Van Aert in the lead group) will drop back to pace him, in an attempt to propel him as high up the GC as possible.September 12, 2026 – 8:40 AMRed Bull offered an interesting quote ahead of the stage today saying that they ‘won't interrupt’ anyone if they were to make a mistake during this tactically complicated stage, and that does indeed appear to be what they were doing when Movistar were panicking earlier. But as the race has settled down, and the chase group built a big lead over the peloton, the Movistar ploy appears to have worked, and they’re back in control of the race. Can Red Bull and their leader Roglič contrive a way to put them under pressure, now that they no longer outnumber Movistar in terms or riders up the road?September 12, 2026 – 8:43 AMWe thought it was coming at some point today, and it's happened already, on the first category one climb of the day with little more than 100km left to ride! It was an explosive move, and he's got a gap, while Decathlon respond by taking over the pace-setting in the peloton. September 12, 2026 – 8:49 AMVan Aert takes the points at the top of the climb, out-sprinting Buitrago's teammate Miguel. He's moved to within 26 points of Buitrago's point tally, and with the group so far behind, he's in with a chance of picking up enough points to take it from him.Further down the mountains, Carapaz has joined Kuss, and 20 seconds behind the peloton is down to only eleven riders - and Mas is isolated. It's all happening on the road!September 12, 2026 – 8:52 AMDecathlon are trying to control this Carapaz attack, but are finding it harder now their key climbing domestique Riccitello has had to pull out of the race. In fact, Gall himself is leading the chase as they summit the climb! Chaos is ensuing a the Vuelta a España September 12, 2026 – 8:57 AMGall sets a ferocious pace up the final kilometres of the climb, dropping everyone bar Roglič and Mas by the summit - and just about manages to bring back Carapaz and Kuss as they go over the top. Onley was dropped just before and is now having to chase as they begin the descent. September 12, 2026 – 9:03 AMA couple of teammates have dropped back from the group ahead to help pace the group of favourites - Carapaz's Albanese, and Kuss' Brennan. Mas, Roglič and Gall are the other riders in the group, while Onley is losing ground, at 20 seconds. September 12, 2026 – 9:10 AMMacKellar has also dropped back to the group of favourites, giving Carapaz another man to set the pace along with Albanese. As the longest valley section left on this stage, this is the ideal time for him to have teammates to set the pace, before they start climbing again in a few kilometres.The move is further distancing Onley behind, who is in a perilous situation but does have Haig to help him, and is also potentially bringing the stage win back into play - the high pace since the Carapaz attack has seen the gap from this group to the leaders come down to about 8:40. September 12, 2026 – 9:19 AMThe riders have begun the second ascent of the Puerto de El Purche, the lead group 8:45 ahead of the group of favourites. The latter keeps picking up riders dropped from the groups ahead, most recently Kuss' teammate Kruijswijk, who is setting the pace.September 12, 2026 – 9:25 AMThis is a picture earlier from MacKellar, back when he was in the main chase group. He's since dropped back, and has just finished doing a long, important turn for Carapaz in the group of favourites.They're putting a lot of time into the group behind, which contains Onley and Omrzel, which is now almost three minutes behind. This is good news especially for Kuss, who stands to shoot up the GC - potentially to as high as fifth overall, if the gap keep increasing at the rate they are. September 12, 2026 – 9:30 AMKuss has gone again! His Visma teammate Kruijswijk had been setting the pace, but now the American has gone solo. There's a slowdown in the GC group, as their positions aren't under threat from Kuss. September 12, 2026 – 9:34 AMGall's teammate Sander De Pestel is the latest rider to drop back, and he's now setting the pace in the group of favourites. It's only a steady pace, though, and Kuss has already built a lead of 30 seconds over them. September 12, 2026 – 9:41 AMVan Aert picks up another ten points at the summit, despite a sprint and desperate lunge from Bahrain's Miguel. He's now left with just 16 points to make up on Van Aert, with ten available on the upcoming climb, and twenty on the final ascent to the finish. He's got a chance!As for the stage win, for all the action behind, the lead group are still over eight minutes ahead of the group of favourites. That's mostly down to the work of Uno-X Mobility, who still have three men working for their elected man for the day, Johannessen.September 12, 2026 – 9:46 AMCarapaz has made another move on the climb! He got a gap, but was brought back by Mas, Gall and Roglič. With a few teammates still up the road in Shaw, Rafferty and Rodriguez, if he can get more of a gap with one of these attacks, he has support up the road to try and build a lead to make a move on the podium. September 12, 2026 – 9:51 AMMost of today's stage has been defined by riders dropping back from out front to the peloton, but we've just had a big name join the front group from behind - Mikel Landa. The veteran has been quiet all Vuelta, but must be on flying form to make up so much ground. Could he claim what would be a romantic stage win?September 12, 2026 – 9:59 AMFor all the action today, the GC remains as you were, with one exception - Sepp Kuss, who is now all the way up to virtual fifth place. He's a long way away from moving further up, but has every chance of maintaining fifth, as Onley and the others are struggling behind without teammates, while Kuss still has Nordhagen and Armirail up the road to help him. September 12, 2026 – 10:06 AMVan Aert slips to the front of the group to add more points in the green jersey classification, but it's the mountain jersey he's after today. Thans to the pace set by Uno-X Mobility, his lead group is still 1:40 up on the Buitrago group, meaning he has a chance of gaining the jersey, if he can win the points at the top of the climb they're about to begin, and finish at last third on the summit finish.If he can do it, Van Aert will become the first rider to win both the points and mountains classification at a Vuelta since María Jiménez in 2001.September 12, 2026 – 10:12 AMThe situation as they ride up the penultimate climb of the day, Puerto de El Duque (7.4km at 8.2%), is that the lead group of 8 (Van Aert, Johannessen, Kron, Dalby, Oliveira, Fisher-Black, Miguel and Landa) are about 6 minutes ahead of Kuss, with many riders in between, and Kuss is 2:30 ahead of the red jersey group (now containing Mas, Roglič, Gall, Carapaz), and 5 minutes ahead of Onley and Omrzel. September 12, 2026 – 10:16 AMThere are more changes on the road: Buitrago has been dropped, and is back in the red jersey group, meaning the defence of his King of the Mountains is now out of his hands, and dependent on Van Aert not claiming enough points. García Pierna is now fulfilling the role he worked so hard earlier in the day to be able to do, and has dropped back to the red jersey group to assist Mas. And ahead, Debruyne has joined Landa in making the juncture from the chase group behind to the lead group. September 12, 2026 – 10:20 AMAll change in the front group on the ultra-steep gradients of Puerto de El Duque! Landa, Johannessen and Debruyne have gone clear of the rest - including Van Aert, who looks set to lose out on the mountains jersey after all.And back in the group of favourites, Red Bull have some teammates (Vermeersch and Thornley) who have dropped back, and are setting the pace for Roglič on the run-in to the final climb. Could this be where he makes his move on the red jersey?September 12, 2026 – 10:21 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 12, 2026 – 10:23 AMRoglič has already burned through his teammates, and is now leading the group instead. It's not an attack, but he's trying to ride a tempo to make Mas uncomfortable. The GC race is on!September 12, 2026 – 10:27 AMCarapaz has a new teammate with him to set the pace on the climb, Juan Felipe Rodriguez, and he's reduced the group to just themselves, Mas, Gall and Roglič. Roglič appears to be struggling, and is has let the smallest of gaps open up between himself and the others on the steep gradients. September 12, 2026 – 10:32 AMCarapaz has tried a couple of attacks the last kilometre or so, but neither were as vicious as earlier. After the first Rodriguez bridged back up to them, and set up a second Carapaz attack, but he again did not succeed in dropping Mas, Gall and Roglič, who are all now riding together. September 12, 2026 – 10:36 AMLanda leads the trio of himself, Debruyne and Johannessen which means Buitrago is now poised to win the KOM jersey, with Van Aert not among the top points.Further down the mountain, the GC riders are playing games with each other, watching each other and riding slowly rather than working together. Gall and Carapaz briefly let a gap grow to the others, but bridged it back. They're calling Mas' bluff - he needs to ride at some point to defend the red jersey from Kuss, who is getting a bigger and bigger gap out front. September 12, 2026 – 10:41 AMCarapaz attacks again, not once but twice, after Rodriguez set him up by increasing the pace again. He might be getting worried about his fourth place on GC, which is coming under pressure from Kuss. Kuss is now almost five minutes ahead of them up the road, which is most of the 5:47 he needs to overtake Carapaz on GC. September 12, 2026 – 10:44 AMAnother of Mas’ teammates up the road, Romeo, has dropped back to the red jersey group and set the pace, controlling it and bringing order after Carapaz’s attacks and leading them over the summit.It might have been a chaotic start, but Movistar have once again ended up playing a tactically astute game, and have things under control - they also have Castrillo up the road for once last teammate to drop back if needed, with just one more climb left to complete. September 12, 2026 – 10:54 AMOne thing that's looking increasingly likely as they approach the final climb is that the stage win will go to one of Landa, Debruyne or Johannessen. They're five minutes ahead of Kuss and 9:40 ahead of the red jersey group, though face more direct threat from Miguel, who is only 30 seconds behind.September 12, 2026 – 11:03 AMJames Shaw is the latest of the apparently infinite number of riders to drop back from the groups in front, and set a pace for Carapaz in the red jersey group. That'll help him defend fourth place from Sepp Kuss (pictured), who now has Van Aert with him and has built a huge lead of 5:30 - nearly enough to overtake Carapaz on GC.September 12, 2026 – 11:06 AMHere we go - the three leaders have started climbing the Collado del Alguacil, which with an average of 9.8%(!) for 8.4km, is the hardest of the entire Vuelta.The red jersey group will start it in about nine minute time, when they arrive at the foot. September 12, 2026 – 11:10 AMLanda is pressing on, and has managed to drop Debruyne. It's now the Spaniard and Johannessen at the front - and Landa is trying to drop him too, with another attack. And he's got a small gap...September 12, 2026 – 11:13 AMLanda has indeed put distance into Johannessen! He now leads the race and appears to be riding to victory, though there are 6 very hard kilometres still to climb.Behind, Van Aert is finished, leaving Kuss to have to pace for himself, but with a big lead of about five and a half minutes over the red jersey group.September 12, 2026 – 11:17 AMIn the red jersey group, Mas' teammate Romeo has been dropped, and Roglič's teammate Finn Fisher-Black is setting the pace on the lower slopes of the mountain. It's not a hard enough pace to put Mas under pressure, though.September 12, 2026 – 11:20 AMLanda is alone in front, and building his lead! Johannessen isn't giving up though, and is still in contention at thirteen seconds behind. In the red jersey group, Mas has help again with Castrillo having dropped back, and now he sets the pace.September 12, 2026 – 11:24 AMStill Castrillo leads the red jersey group. This is looking very good for Mas, and no attacks are forthcoming from his rivals in the group, with the kilometres running out. September 12, 2026 – 11:27 AMKuss now has Nordhagen to help pace him, and is over four minutes ahead of the red jersey group. He doesn't look set to gain enough time to move into the top four, but fifth place is surely his.September 12, 2026 – 11:30 AMAs Castrillo finishes his turn, Gall tries an attack for the first time today - and its an effective one! He's dropped everyone besides Mas. The Austrian needs 1:24 to take over Roglič in second place on GC.September 12, 2026 – 11:33 AMGall has now gapped Mas, by a few seconds! It's too little too late if he had designs on the red jersey, though - or the stage win, which Landa is 500m away from sealing. September 12, 2026 – 11:35 AMMikel Landa solos to the top of the mountain, to take a beautiful victory! It's his first for years, and a wonderful moment for a rider who has had a really difficult season. September 12, 2026 – 11:37 AMJohannessen takes second, and Debruyne third, to complete the podium for the stage.Behind, Mas is in the rare position of having been dropped, and Gall is growing his lead. But he's not going to gain the 3:01 he needs to overtake him at the top of the GC.September 12, 2026 – 11:40 AMKuss has just finished, with his teammate Norhagen. He has surely done enough to move up to 5th on GC - what a final stage for the American, who started it in 11th. September 12, 2026 – 11:42 AMNow Gall finishes, but Mas has him in his sights, and will finish just a few seconds behind.The big question is: where is Roglič? And can he defend his second-place on GC from Gall?September 12, 2026 – 11:44 AMRoglič finishes, and has indeed done enough to maintain his second overall. And shortly after so does Richard Carapaz, in time to defend his fourth place on GC from Sepp Kuss. The headline story though is of course, that Enric Mas has all but won the Vuelta a España!September 12, 2026 – 11:49 AMWhat a day for Mikel Landa. Remarkably, he hadn't won a race of any kind for over five years, and not at Grand Tour level for almost a decade. That was a comprehensive rebuttal of anyone who has written him off. September 12, 2026 – 11:53 AMLanda might be considered the best GC rider in the world not to have won a Grand Tour - a label he had shared with Enric Mas. But not any more! After another brilliant performance in the mountains, from both himself and his Movistar team, Mas looks set to wrap up overall victory in Granada tomorrow, with an increased lead of 2:15 over Primož Roglič in second. September 12, 2026 – 11:58 AMAfter his impressive attack on the final, we can’t help but wonder what might have been if Gall had attacked earlier in the stage. As Sepp Kuss demonstrated, the race was chaotic enough to potentially make big gains on GC, if gaps were opened up earlier; perhaps if he had worked with Carapaz when he was making his earlier attacks, rather than rae to defend against him, he might have been able to at least put Mas under pressure. Instead, he only gained a handful of seconds on the red jersey, and not enough either on Roglič to move up to second place. As impressive as third place at the Vuelta is, it might have been more with a more aggressive and ambitious approach. September 12, 2026 – 12:04 PMMikel Landa (Spa) Soudal Quick-StepTobias Johannessen (Nor) Uno-X MobilityRamses Debryne (Bel) Alpecin-Premier TechPau Miquel Delgado (Spa) Bahrain VictoriousUrko Berrade Fernandez (Spa) Kern PharmaJan Hirt (Cze) NSN CyclingJørgen Nordhagen (Nor) Visma-Lease A BikeSepp Kuss (USA) Visma-Lease A BikeWalter Calzoni (Ita) Pinarello-Q36.5Lorenzo Fortunato (Ita) XDS AstanaSeptember 12, 2026 – 12:08 PMPrimoz Roglic (Slo) Red Bull-Bora-HansgroheFélix Gall (Aut) Decathlon CMA CGMRichard Carapaz (Ecu) EF Education-EasyPostSepp Kuss (USA) Visma-Lease A BikeOscar Onley (GBr) Netcompany IneosJakob Omrzel (Slo) Bahrain VictoriousClément Berthet (Fra) Groupama-FDJ UnitedCristian Rodriguez (Spa) XDS AstanaSeptember 12, 2026 – 12:25 PMOne of the sub-plots of the way was Van Aert's attempt to win the King of the Mountains ahead of Santiago Buitrago. Ultimately he didn't quite have the climbing legs, but will still win the points classification if he finishes tomorrow's final stage.September 12, 2026 – 12:30 PMThanks for joining us today, for what was a magnificent stage for Spanish cycling. Not only did Mikel Landa enjoy one of the best day's of his long career, claiming the queen stage of the race with a magnificent ride, but Enric Mas all but sealed the nation's first home overall victory at the Vuelta since 2014. These two riders have endured their fair share of hardships over the years, but every dog has its day, and both enjoyed just that on stage 20.Be sure to join us again tomorrow, where Mas will enjoy his victory lap as champion of the Vuelta, and the best stage-hunters of the race will do battle for one more win on what looks like a thrilling circuit on the streets of Granada.

item.title: ‘We can see into the other room’: insurers face surge in subsidence claims
item.author: Julia Kollewe
item.content:encoded: Stressed UK homeowners tell of cracks opening up in the walls around them after two record-hot summers“We’ve got one wall with an absolutely huge diagonal crack, through which we can see through to the other room; you could easily put your fingers in it and chunks of plaster are falling off,” says Henry Biggs, 49, from Stroud in Gloucestershire.He and his partner started noticing cracks in their family home in June 2025, a few months after buying it, and filed an insurance claim for subsidence that was accepted by their insurer, Admiral, in the spring. Monitoring devices were only recently fitted, about a year after they first submitted the claim, and they have no idea when the damage might start to be repaired.Continue reading...

item.title: MotoGP San Marino GP: Bezzecchi beats Marquez for record-breaking pole
item.content:encoded: Marco Bezzecchi smashed the Misano circuit record to claim his second consecutive pole position of the 2026 MotoGP season at the San Marino Grand Prix.The factory Aprilia rider posted an incredible time of 1m29.982s on his first run in qualifying, beating reigning MotoGP champion Marc Marquez to the top spot by almost two tenths of a second.Gresini’s Fermin Aldeguer came from Q1 to ...Keep reading

item.title: New Misano lap record from Bezzecchi as he beats Marquez to pole
item.author: Valentin Khorounzhiy
item.content:encoded: MotoGP title hopeful Marco Bezzecchi dominated qualifying for the San Marino Grand Prix at Misano, seeing off his main rival this weekend Marc Marquez.A first-ever 1m29s MotoGP lap of Misano - replacing Pecco Bagnaia's 2024 time as the new record, and set in the wheeltracks of Aprilia team-mate and points leader Jorge Martin - propelled Bezzecchi to a huge lead early on in Q2, and meant he didn't have to risk on the second run.Though the gap was whittled down by the end, nobody got close to Bezzecchi's 1m29.982s.Marquez bounced back from a mistake early on his second run to deliver the second-fastest lap of the session, two tenths down on Bezzecchi, with Fermin Aldeguer a surprise third for Gresini Ducati.Aldeguer worked his way through Q1 on his year-old Ducati and found another two tenths between sessions to score his second front row of the year.Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Ducati) crashed late on but still took fourth, ahead of Martin - whose last-lap attempt went awry at Tramonto - and Honda standout Luca Marini.Pedro Acosta again led the KTM contingent in seventh, ahead of Di Giannantonio's team-mate Franco Morbidelli, who will serve a long-lap penalty on Sunday for having impeded Enea Bastianini on Friday.Two Q2 crashes meant a frustrated Alex Marquez could do no better than ninth, but he still outpaced Raul Fernandez (who would have been fifth had he matched his Q1 time), Johann Zarco and Pol Espargaro.Fabio Quartararo led the Yamaha contingent by six tenths but just didn't have the sectors three-and-four performance to challenge for the top two in Q1, ending up a quarter of a second back in 13th.He was followed in the order by Bagnaia, who never looked like a big threat for Q2 - even before he scuffed up four successive laps on his second run in Q1.1 Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia) 1m29.982s2 Marc Marquez (Ducati) +0.198s3 Fermin Aldeguer (Gresini Ducati) +0.368s4 Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Ducati) +0.404s5 Jorge Martin (Aprilia) +0.587s6 Luca Marini (Honda) +0.627s7 Pedro Acosta (KTM) +0.658s8 Franco Morbidelli (VR46 Ducati) +0.661s9 Alex Marquez (Gresini Ducati) +0.714s10 Raul Fernandez (Trackhouse Aprilia) +0.871s11 Johann Zarco (LCR Honda) +0.905s12 Pol Espargaro (Tech3 KTM) +1.198s13 Fabio Quartararo (Yamaha) +0.222s to Q214 Francesco Bagnaia (Ducati) +0.339s15 Diogo Moreira (LCR Honda) +0.389s16 Enea Bastianini (Tech3 KTM) +0.536s17 Joan Mir (Honda) +0.572s18 Jack Miller (Pramac Yamaha) +0.836s19 Brad Binder (KTM) +0.975s20 Alex Rins (Yamaha) +1.016s21 Toprak Razgatlioglu (Pramac Yamaha) +1.687s

item.title: China’s AI Industry Pivots to Agents From Models, Report Says
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: China’s artificial intelligence industry is shifting from competition in large models and computing power toward the deployment and commercialization of AI agents, according to a report by the China Telecom Research Institute cited by China Central Television on Saturday.

item.title: Today on Pinstripe Alley – 9/12/26
item.author: Andrew Mearns

item.title: F1's TV visuals are letting its Madrid track down
item.author: Edd Straw
item.content:encoded: Television doesn't do the Madring justice. It's a spectacular place to watch Formula 1 cars, which was clear from heading trackside during FP1 and visiting various vantage points in the first half of the lap during the session. Yet following FP2 from the media centre with sight of the world feed it looked like an entirely different - blander - venue. Partly, that is the curse of such 'urban' circuits. The nature of such facilities means endless fences, barriers punctuated only by occasional bridges branded by Pirelli, American Express et al, which dominate what fans at home see. It also leaves little room to manoeuvre when it comes to camera positions in terms of space, especially given the need to ensure they offer clean backdrops that aren't polluted by some of the necessary temporary infrastructure such as Portaloos.This makes it difficult to showcase a circuit that, while certainly no Suzuka or Spa, is a very worthy addition to the calendar. "A commitment track" is how Charles Leclerc characterised it, and that's exactly what drivers and fans desire from the driving challenge of a new circuit. Yet the onboard cameras, which usually sanitise and stabilise the experience, are forced to do the heavy lifting.It's a privileged position to be able to get up close to the cars when they are running - and this isn’t about arguing viewers should appreciate what they can't see. But while the coverage is, for all the criticisms, excellent (check out a broadcast from 30 years ago to see how far it has come), it's the alpha and omega when it comes to showcasing F1. You cannot build excitement and enthusiasm for a first grand prix, then show it off so poorly.There's an unavoidable flattening effect from filming that is impossible to get around, and no matter how many races you see from Spa before you visit, your reaction to seeing the steep incline of Eau Rouge in person will always take your breath away. This means the elevation change at Madring will be subdued on screen. But what doesn't come over so well is just how unforgiving it is, giving drivers little or no margin for error in many places where there can be big laptime gains, or losses, in committing that little bit more. This side of Madring should be experienced by everyone, not just those on the ground.The banked corner of La Monumental is a great example. Conceived as a Mexico stadium-style cauldron, where spectators crowd the corner, it is a uniquely long turn with big consequences should things go wrong - yet it becomes flat on TV. The low angle and the not-quite-high-enough elevated angle diminish its grandeur. And parts of the track resemble just another Miami/Sochi-style venue.Part of that is the surroundings. It's built in and around the IFEMA exhibition centre, which by definition will comprise large halls and their infrastructure. In some ways, this is used well with the distinctive indoor team trucks/engineering hubs (as opposed to the hospitality units, which are outside). But it poses limitations because the environs are, fundamentally, bland. There's little that screams 'Madrid' about it, partly because it's outlying rather than in the city centre.It will improve next year, even if no conscious action is taken - because the Madring will have had time to bed in, it will be tidier and cleaner. Camera locations and views will be optimised and that should at least close the gap. None of this is easy and plenty of effort will have already gone into showing it off well, but there must also be some serious thinking in how to present a charismatic circuit that genuinely adds something unique to the calendar more faithfully. The design of the ribbon of asphalt is the key part of any F1 newcomer, and Madring has done a good job with that, but more can be done to show that to the outside world.

item.content:encoded: The World Cup and its aftermath made clear that Fifa needs independent oversight by governments and NGOs dedicated to preserving the people’s gameThe 2026 World Cup was a whirling swirl of scintillating soccer that prompted much-needed conversations about the vitality of diaspora, the fortitude of the underdog, the power of sport. In a world fractured along myriad cultural axes floating in an entertainment system dominated by on-demand content, the tournament provided a moment, perhaps unlike any other event, that brought together people from different backgrounds to simultaneously experience something meaningful.After the tournament concluded, Fifa president Gianni Infantino dropped a political pipebomb into the after-party, proposing to privatize the World Cup by injecting $20bn in private capital, with an assist from JP Morgan and Thrive Capital, the investment vehicle orchestrated by Joshua Kushner, brother to Jared Kushner, Donald Trump’s son-in-law.Continue reading...

item.title: Yankees news: Remembering September 11th
item.author: Matt Ferenchick
item.content:encoded: ABC7 | Sam Ryan: Yesterday was the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks, and baseball played somewhat of a role in helping New York and the nation emotionally recover. Several players from 2001 were part of the pregame remembrances ahead of the Subway Series game on Friday. Players from both teams also took time to tell what they remember from those times 25 years ago.MLB.com | Bryan Hoch: Among those pregame moments, the Yankees had Brielle Saracini and Sean McGuire, who were both children when they lost parents on 9/11 (and later married), throw out the first pitches. However, it was not Saracini’s first time up close with the Yankees, as Derek Jeter and the team invited her to a game back in 2001 after she had written a letter to the team as a 10-year old shortly after the tragedy. Ahead of Friday’s game, they reunited and both remembered their experiences.New York Post | Dan Martin: The Yankees made a couple lower-profile additions to try and shore up their bullpen in recent weeks, and one of them was former AL Rookie of the Year Michael Fulmer. In this Subway Series, he’s facing the team that drafted him years ago, eventually trading him to the Tigers for Yoenis Cespedes in 2015. However, he’s now on the other side of the city and has gotten off to a decent start in the Bronx.

item.title: F1 teams face big Madring strategy dilemma
item.author: Jon Noble
item.content:encoded: Formula 1 isn't really heading for the six-stopper Spanish Grand Prix that George Russell half joked was on the cards after opening practice.But tyre supplier Pirelli says a combination of factors at F1's newest venue means strategy is going to be particularly tricky to work out.In fact, the initial prediction following Friday's running is that teams are going to be stuck between a rock and a hard place when working out what is best to do.The super-long pitlane, which has left the pitstop loss time at around 24 seconds, is a deterrent for tyre changes and means the most logical route should be a one-stopper.But high levels of thermal degradation of the rubber, and particularly challenging front left graining, means that a two-stop would be sensible.With no middle ground between those two choices, it is not going to be a case of what is the best strategy to pick. It is about which is the least bad.F1 teams were left wide-eyed after opening practice when the tyre degradation looked pretty extreme.A combination of high grip asphalt (highest of the season according to Pirelli), a smooth surface and fast corners has meant cars are sliding a lot – and that triggered some alarming findings during that first session.As Russell said: "It's often a possibility on new tarmacs that the grip is very high but you're sliding quite aggressively."With the deg we had in FP1, a six-stop race would have been the fastest way. FP2 was slightly better and I'm sure the race on Sunday will be better again. But that's the biggest question mark." From Pirelli's perspective, there are two issues that drivers and teams are going to have to manage as the Spanish GP weekend continues – and neither is particularly straightforward.The most complex issue is front left graining, which is being generated because the combination of the smooth surface and high grip means the rubber hits peak stress easily and the surface effectively tears.Front graining triggers mid-corner understeer and a subsequent drop in performance. It is much harder to manage on the kind of high-speed corners that feature at the Madring than it is at low-speed venues.Oscar Piastri said after Friday that this element had been the biggest headache from running."It's been a nightmare to try and manage the tyres with graining," he said. "It normally gets better through a weekend, but we'll have to wait and see how much better."It is not just the fronts that are proving to be hard to deal with around the Madring, because the high-speed corners and the way the cars are almost constantly in turns means that the rears are overheating too.Throw these two elements together and the result is high degradation.Pirelli chief engineer Simone Berra reckoned that the drop off here was at a "very high" level – around 0.2-0.3 seconds per lap based on some of the long runs in FP2."It was a surprise to have these kinds of values," he said. "They were outside our range of expectations."While general track evolution and improved set-ups should help reduce that figure by the time the race comes around, the scene is set for the Spanish GP turning into a race where tyre strategy will be critical.That is what has fuelled all teams apart from Audi electing to keep two hard tyres back after Friday practice – as that could well be the most resilient option for Sunday.Berra said that the unpredictability thrown up by the front graining and overheating, plus the levels of the degradation, meant that plotting the right path through the race was going to be tough to nail."I don't want to exclude any kind of situation," he said. "I think looking from the data, you would think that the teams will go for a two-stop because the degradation is very high."But the pitstop loss is 24 seconds, so I'm pretty sure that some teams will try to reach as a target the one-stop race."It means we could end up in different situations, with some teams trying the one-stop and other teams trying the two-stops."Which route is best is unclear right now, and matters are further complicated by how difficult it could be to overtake.For even though the new power units mean deployment offsets can make passes easier at some venues than in the past, equally there are downsides to falling into the pack.Berra added: "If you are in traffic, you lose quite a lot of performance, and you also destroy your tyres because you lose load and you generate high temperatures as you're sliding."So, we have different factors that are pushing teams towards different directions. "It's not easy; in fact, it is pretty complicated."
