item.title: 'I would love to do my first Grand Tour' - US talent Artem Shmidt trades Netcompany Ineos for NSN Cycling
item.author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
item.content:encoded: His victory at the 1.Pro race in France on a rainy May edition saw him make an aggressive solo move to disrupt an expected battle of sprinters. His power, combined with tactical acumen, cast a sharp light on his growing versatility. “Artem Shmidt is one of the most exciting talents to come out of the US in recent years, and we believe he represents a rider profile we don’t currently have in the team,” said Kjell Carlstrom, NSN's general manager, in a press release Friday.“Artem already has some very clear qualities, particularly in the time trial, but what excites us is how much more he can develop over the next three seasons. He only has two seasons in the WorldTour to his name, and already he has shown great potential, so a big objective for us is to continue facilitating that development and see just how far he can go in one-day and stage races."Shmidt has developed from his junior years with LUX Cycling and Hot Tubes Development for two years on the Continental level with Hagens Berman Jayco. He was always comfortable and strong on a time trial bike, winning his first USPro title in the men's U23 ITT in 2024, then sweeping the elite title the next two years.A move to NSN is now an opportunity for Shmidt to develop for stage racing, his goal to earn a spot for a Grand Tour appearance, which would be his first.“In terms of my development in road racing, I believe NSN is the perfect team for me to develop an aggressive and opportunistic racing style and really sharpen those characteristics I have shown as a rider. My big objectives will naturally be the time trials and Spring Classics, but I would love to do my first Grand Tour," Shmidt said in the NSN announcement about his new contract."There were many things that stood out to me about NSN Cycling Team. The professionalism and the way the team came across in our meetings were important, but what really made an impact was the culture. The English-speaking environment and the atmosphere in the team were big factors for me, and the racing style is more my type of beat. "Being up the road, attacking, and on that front foot is the mentality that we share.”Shmidt will compete at Grands Prix Cyclistes Québec et Montréal for Netcompany Ineos and follow the Canadian doubleheader by representing Team USA at UCI Road World Championships in Montréal, riding in the elite men's time trial and road race.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!

item.title: Buddhist monk arrested in Thailand on suspicion of embezzling $2.8m
item.author: Agence France-Press in Bangkok
item.content:encoded: Phra Wachirayan Wi arrested alongside woman he was filmed having sex with in latest scandal to hit country’s clergyPolice in Thailand have arrested a senior Buddhist monk on suspicion of embezzling $2.8m intended for his monastery, alongside a suspected female accomplice he was filmed having sex with.The case is the latest scandal to hit the clergy in the Buddhist-majority country, after a sex and extortion case involving senior monks last year prompted public outrage and calls for greater scrutiny of temple finances.Continue reading...

item.title: Dementia patients warned off seeking home care in case Australia’s aged care algorithm cuts funding
item.author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
item.content:encoded: FoI documents show senior health officials were warned of concerns about assessment tool weeks after it launchedPeople with dementia were warned not to apply for home support because of fears their care would be downgraded by the government’s aged care algorithm.Documents released to Guardian Australia under freedom of information (FoI) laws reveal the warnings came within weeks of the November rollout of the algorithm, which is used to determine funding packages and priority of need for older Australians requiring home support.Continue reading...

item.title: Decathlon CMA CGM register for business in Switzerland – Could contractual benefits help them keep Paul Seixas?
item.author: Patrick Fletcher
item.content:encoded: The Decathlon CMA CGM team has registered for business in Switzerland, switching its paying agent from France in a move that’s understood to be linked to their fight to keep hold of their prized rider, Paul Seixas, in the long-term. The possibility of such a switch, which would save considerable sums of money in taxes, was first raised in the spring, but denied by the team management at the time. It has now come to fruition.A new entity has been listed at the Register of Commerce in Geneva, named 'DECATHLON CYCLING TEAM SUISSE SA'. Registered on August 17, it carries the names of the team’s two senior management figures, Dominique Serieys and Mathieu Charpentier, and concerns ‘the management and activity of a professional cycling team’. A spokesperson for the team has confirmed to that this will be the new company that operates the cycling team from 2027. In addition to the men’s WorldTour squad, this entity will also govern the team’s development squads and a new women’s team that’s launching in 2027.The team insist they are still a French outfit, and they will continue to be a French-registered team when it comes to their WorldTour license with the UCI. In addition, their headquarters will remain where they are in La Motte-Servolex, near the French Alps. What’s changing is the legal and administrative base of the company that runs the team, often referred to in cycling as the ‘paying agent’. All contracts, therefore, will be arranged according to Swiss law. The team have declined to comment on the reasons for this change. It is one that will come with a considerable financial benefit. It will, for starters, mean the team will not pay the higher level of social security contributions that are associated with French contracts. Marc Madiot, president of the French team Groupama-FDJ, has previously highlighted this uneven playing field, suggesting a rule whereby all teams must have their base in Switzerland, where the UCI operates. Where Seixas comes into this is that Decathlon CMA CGM will effectively be able to offer him a higher salary, as a lesser percentage of it would be going to the taxman. There has been intense speculation over Seixas’ future this spring as he has stormed to very top echelon of the sport with a string of astounding performances at just 19 years of age. As Tadej Pogačar dominates the sport, teams are queuing up for the next best thing and Decathlon have been facing a fight to keep him beyond his current contract, which expires at the end of 2027. Having already been aggressive in the transfer market this summer, this move will in theory allow them to be more competitive when it comes to offering him a new package. But it’s not just down to Seixas. The team has been growing in stature since the Decathlon came on board as a sponsor in 2022, and then took over full ownership of the team from AG2R La Mondiale at the start of this year.The injection of investment from the international sports retailing giant has already seen them referred to among the ‘super-team’ bracket of cycling’s WorldTour, and the move to Switzerland will only hone their financial muscle. item.title: Record Watch: Five Knicks benchmarks in jeopardy this season
item.author: John Gove
item.content:encoded: Defending a championship changes the vibe during regular-season play. When the goal is to repeat a championship in June, Tuesday night games in February can feel like a formality. Nobody wants to overexert a key player in a meaningless game on the off chance that he’ll blow a hammy. However, Mike Brown’s offense, built for another deep playoff run, can’t help but generate eye-popping stats all season long.Between the exploding scoreboards, higher possession counts, and New York’s elite playmakers and scorers, several Knicks records are suddenly at risk. Some of these benchmarks have survived nearly 40 years, while the ink for others is still wet in the books. A closer look at the roster and statistics suggests five specific franchise records could realistically fall this season. Let’s dive in.Single-Season 30-Point GamesCurrent Record: 36 games – Richie Guerin (1961-1962), Patrick Ewing (1989-90), Jalen Brunson (2023-24)2026-27 Season Target: 37 gamesThe current franchise mark for the most 30-point contest in a regular season is a three-way tie spanning three distinct eras of Knicks basketball. Richie Guerin established the benchmark during the fast-break pace of the early 1960s. Patrick Ewing matched it during his prime, dominating the post game-in and game-out while carrying the team on his broad shoulders and aching knees. Captain Jalen Brunson joined the two Hall of Famers two seasons ago during his rise to All-NBA status.Of every record on this list, this one is the most wobbly. Brunson remains the undisputed engine of New York’s half-court offense, combining incredible footwork with elite basketball smarts.In Mike Brown’s five-out system, defenses can no longer load up in the paint without leaving deadly perimeter shooters uncovered. Having Karl-Anthony Towns at center pulls defensive anchors 25 feet away from the basket, giving Brunson wider driving lanes, fewer double-teams, and access to his mid-range spots. Assuming he’ll be healthy all season (knock on wood and cross yourself), Brunson claiming sole possession of this record with 37-plus 30-point games feels more like a matter of when, not if.Single-Game Scoring RecordCurrent Record: 62 points – Carmelo Anthony (January 24, 2014 vs. Charlotte Bobcats)2026-27 Season Target: 63 pointsFirst, a moment of silence for the Charlotte Bobcats. . . . Okay, we’re good to go.Carmelo Anthony’s 62-point masterclass against Charlotte has stood untouched for 13 years. In a legendary isolation clinic, Melo shot 23-of-35 from the floor without recording a single assist or turnover. Surpassing a single-game point total like that requires the blend of crazy shot volume, incredible efficiency, (no small degree of selfishness,) and a game that’s competitive enough to keep starters on the floor late into the fourth quarter.New York’s current roster is different because it features distinct creators who can completely go off in a single game. Brunson already came within a single point of the record, dropping 61 points on 47 shot attempts against the Spurs in March 2024. Meanwhile, Towns brings a personal career-high of 62 points from his time in Minnesota, with an outside stroke that can cause box score chaos. If Towns hits six or seven early threes while dominating the glass, or if Brunson takes over a high-paced track meet, Carmelo’s iconic record could melt like a stick of butter on a sunny afternoon.Single Season Team 3-PointersCurrent Record: 1,168 made three-pointers (2025-26)2026-27 Season Target: 1,169 made three-pointersNew York set a new record last season, draining 1,168 three-pointers. And Mike Brown’s Knicks are just getting started.Brown’s scheme relies heavily on five-out principles that are designed to distort perimeter coverage. With movement shooters on the bench (Shamet, McBride, and occasionally Alvarado and Clarkson), the sheer volume of perimeter attempts is bound to increase. Averaging roughly 14 made threes a game across a full schedule, and thereby breaking their own team record for a second straight season, seems like the natural trajectory for this squad.Individual Single Season 3-PointersCurrent Record: 283 made three-pointers – Donte DiVincenzo (2023-24 season)2026-27 Season Target: 284 made three-pointersWhen Donte DiVincenzo poured in 283 three-pointers during his lone full season with the Knicks, he shattered Evan Fournier’s previous mark of 241, setting an incredible bar for perimeter volume. Reaching that total requires a player to average roughly 3.5 made threes per game while appearing in almost every matchup.DiVincenzo and Fournier are long gone, but the team has redistributed the heavy perimeter workload across its primary offensive tools. Both Towns and Brunson shoot near 40% from beyond the arc and often get the green light in Brown’s system. If KAT maintains a high-volume, trailing-center role in transition, or if Cap takes even more off-dribble pull-up jumpers, DiVo’s record could easily be squashed before the season’s end.Single Season Point TotalCurrent Record: 2,347 points – Patrick Ewing (1989-90 season)2026-27 Season Target: 2,348 pointsEwing’s 1989-90 campaign remains the ultimate test of single-season scoring in franchise history. Piling up 2,347 total points, Ewing averaged 28.6 points per contest and played all 82 games. Obviously, the big fella served as the team’s primary generator and carried most of the load that year.Surpassing Ewing’s record is hands-down the most grueling challenge on this list of beatable benchmarks. Per-game averages mean little if a player misses games due to load management or minor injury, so any absence from the floor will interrupt the scoring pace needed to top Patrick. Across 77 appearances in 2023-24, Brunson recorded 2,212 points, which put him within spitting distance of the record. To beat out Ewing, Jalen would need to maintain a scoring average north of 28 points per game, while playing in at least 80 contests. Requiring a combination of elite offensive production and availability, the 2,348 points in a season is the hardest to crack, and as Jalen enters his thirties, Coach Brown is likely to play Jalen for shorter stints in unimportant games, to preserve him for the offseason. Still, it is mathematically within reach.Some franchise records are so incredible that they’re unlikely to be toppled, given the changes in play-style, rules, and rosters over time. However, Mike Brown’s team, based on a high-volume, high-efficiency attack, is not your father’s Knicks. In the 1995-96 season, the ‘Bockers averaged 97.2 points per game and attempted 1,285 three-pointers; thirty years later, they averaged 116.5 PPG and took 3,133 threes. And that’s not even top-five in the league! (The Warriors tried 3,616.) With the firepower currently employed at MSG, some of these historical benchmarks are truly at risk.Which records do you think will fall this year? Talk about it below!

item.title: ClickFix attacks infecting PCs and Macs are going viral
item.author: Dan Goodin
item.content:encoded: It wasn’t that long ago that ClickFix attacks were exotic. Now the technique has become mainstream as attackers reap its simplicity and effectiveness in infecting users of PCs and Macs alike. All that’s required is a compromised website—a painless enough task—a fake CAPTCHA overlay, and the inclusion of a single terminal command. So many visitors get suckered into pasting and running the command that just about every malware pusher has adopted the technique. Even Kremlin-backed hacking groups are joining in.“Reddit is becoming post after post after post of people getting their computer infected via ClickFix,” independent researcher Kevin Beaumont observed Thursday. “Legit websites everywhere [are] getting hacked to serve the fake captcha prompts.”How many of us make things worseMore seasoned Internet users—a fair number who read this site—are quick to dismiss the attack. They typically blame the people who fall for the scams and marvel at their gullibility and lack of attention. The reality is that for more casual users, using computers and the Internet has become so difficult—think impossible-to-close interstitials, CAPTCHAs with an endless series of pictures to analyze, and constantly changing interfaces that bury the features they’re looking for—that they have grown desensitized to instructions that seem ridiculous and burdensome.

item.title: What happens when quantum mechanics and relativity meet?
item.author: Jacek Krywko
item.content:encoded: Almost a hundred years ago, physicists theorized out what free fall should do to a quantum wave. If the solution they came up with is wrong, quantum mechanics and Einstein's theory of gravity flatly contradict each other. But testing it has been impossible because nobody has managed to build an interferometer that could perform the necessary measurement.Now, a team led by Ron Folman, a physicist at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, with collaborators in Germany, the UK, and the US, including Nobel laureate Roger Penrose, has done it. They built a new interferometer that gives a single atom two possible paths at once: one that involves a free fall, and another where it is held perfectly still. Both paths end at the same place at the same moment, allowing the team to measure what the fall does to a wave-like property of the atom.Ever since Galileo, physicists have known how to describe a falling object—where it is, how fast it goes, or how quickly it accelerates. Quantum mechanics, though, insists that every object is also a wave. “Every particle, doesn't matter if it's a car or a spaceship or an atom, is a wave,” Folman says. “Everything that is a wave, like sea waves or sound waves, goes up and down. And if you're up or down, this is measured by something called a phase. A phase just tells you if you are at the top of the wave or at the bottom.”

item.title: Could United Launch Alliance's money problems finally force its owners to sell?
item.author: Stephen Clark
item.content:encoded: Pretty much every rocket company in the United States, save one, has embraced two fundamental tenets: reusability and diversification.Most famously, SpaceX branched out from reusable rockets to pursue and dominate a growing spectrum of space services: cargo delivery, human spaceflight, satellite production, broadband, and, perhaps soon, orbital data centers and in-space manufacturing. Blue Origin is evolving from a pure rocket company into a satellite manufacturer, robotics developer, and, most recently, a potential competitor for SpaceX's Starlink network.Rocket Lab used a different approach to diversify after achieving success with its small Electron launch vehicle. The company relocated its headquarters from New Zealand to Southern California, started building spacecraft and payloads, and then went on a spree of corporate acquisitions to expand into satellite communications and take on a new role as a merchant supplier of satellite components and sensors. It's now in a stage of advanced development of its partially reusable next-generation Neutron launch vehicle.

item.title: Rocket Report: Europe joins the commercial launch club; a Ravn X sighting?
item.author: Eric Berger
item.content:encoded: Welcome to Edition 9.10 of the Rocket Report! This week we're celebrating a historic moment in Europe when a German rocket company successfully put its launch vehicle into orbit. Isar Aerospace became the first purely commercial European company to reach orbit, and impressively it did so on just its second launch attempt. How quickly can they scale up operations? How quickly will the second European launch firm reach this goal? Big questions, which for now we don't have answers to.As always, we welcome reader submissions, and if you don't want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar.Isar Aerospace takes a huge step forward. Isar Aerospace, founded in 2018 by three students at a German university, successfully launched a privately developed rocket into low-Earth orbit on Saturday from a Norwegian spaceport inside the Arctic Circle. The two-stage rocket, Spectrum, became the first fully commercial launch vehicle in Europe to reach orbit, Ars reports. With Saturday’s success, Isar becomes the clear leader among a pack of several European launch startups vying to inject some competition into Europe’s stagnant launch market.

item.title: Curse of the Nile’s gold: how Sudan is losing its fertile fields and ability to produce food
item.author: Samira Hassan Khalifa in Abu Hamad
item.content:encoded: An artisanal mining boom driven by war and poverty is causing a public health emergency, as chemicals poison soil, water and societyIn Abu Hamad, on the banks of the Nile, verdant orchards, gardens and fields once produced a bounty of dates, citrus fruits, winter grains and cereals for the towns and cities of eastern Sudan, including Khartoum and Port Sudan.Today, the land looks drastically different. Trees have been cut down, agricultural areas cleared, and farms have been replaced by shops and commercial sites. Dotted around the town and its outskirts, more than 700 mounds of grey waste are poisoning the soil, water and air. The mounds are the toxic remnants of artisanal gold mining, a practice that began in about 2008 and has intensified over the past six years.Continue reading...

item.title: 'The last year I don't think we've done a single aero test' –Why time trials are no longer a major focus for Primož Roglič and why the Vuelta TT did not go as Red Bull predicted
item.author: James Moultrie
item.content:encoded: Just 1km shorter than Thursday's TT at La Vuelta, Roglič gained 1:38 over the Spaniard on that day. If they wanted to completely overhaul Mas and take the red jersey, they were going to need more – 2:10 to be precise – after Mas had eked out his advantage with superiority in the mountains.When the dust settled on Roglič's and Mas' efforts into Jerez, there was to be no miracle switch, with the red jersey defending his lead superbly to finish just 33 seconds slower than the rival who has long been beating him at the Vuelta. What had gone wrong for Roglič? In reality, not much. When his sports directors came to speak to the press, Sven Vanthourenhout stressed how he had done 'everything perfect', which team Head of Engineering Dan Bigham confirmed was the numerical truth, not just the right answer at the time from the team. It was more a case of Mas riding the TT of his career, much as he claimed this was not the case, but it's fair to say Red Bull were not expecting the gap between the two to be so relatively narrow."Roglič had a good last sector, but then, to be honest, so did Mas, and he really outperformed our models, which is reflective of where Mas is in the race, and you can't really ignore it," Bigham told outside the packed Red Bull team bus on Thursday. "He has been by some margin the best climber, and today did his best time trial probably ever, I would say actually, [but] I need to check the numbers and see how it pans out."But [Felix] Gall was within about 10 seconds or so versus our prediction. Callum [Thornley] was actually a second slower. Roglič was seven seconds quicker. Finn [Fisher-Black] was nine seconds quicker. So we're within 10 seconds on most of our predictions for the guys who have numbers on, and yeah, Mas was just a whole lot faster than probably you would have stuck a number on three weeks ago."Given the context of not being able to train on his TT bike before the Vuelta at all, due to being hit by a driver in training near Livigno, Roglič himself was delighted with the performance, simply conceding that Mas was untouchable for the moment. Two mountain stages remain, but what we've seen ever since Mas inherited red is that there's a considerable gap between the two when it comes to climbing. The time trial was Roglič's big chance. Time trials no longer a major focus for RogličRoglič remains in the upper echelon, but was once one of the absolute best time trial riders in the world, winning eight Grand Tour ITT stages down the years, an Olympic title in Tokyo, and finishing second at the World Championships in 2017.There was talk at the start of Roglič not riding the same developmental model of Specialized TT bike that Remco Evenepoel had access to at the Tour. But Bigham also revealed the lack of time the Slovenian has been dedicating to time trialling in what will be his final year on Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe. "So in my first year, I worked with him quite a bit, and we did quite a lot of testing," Bigham told . "To be honest, the last year, I don't think we've done a single aero test, which is probably more of a reflection on where he feels he is in his position and what evolution he wants or doesn't want, and also what he wants to focus on. "Obviously, family is one big important thing for him, but also at the same time, his ambitions require him to just train a lot. And his opinion was he didn't think he could evolve his position any further, so he wasn't that fussed by doing more testing."While it's an important point to note, and perhaps could have meant for a few seconds gained here and there on the course on Thursday, Bigham was certain that it wouldn't have done much in the way of pulling back the extra time he required to really move closer to Mas' hold on red."No, not particularly," he said when asked whether the change in focus was a major factor. "No, I don't think if I'd spent more time with him, we would have found – what did we need, 90 seconds? So yeah, I mean 90 seconds on this course-that's about 45 watts. I'm not finding 45 watts. That's about 12% drag reduction. I can dream of that, but yeah."Focusing on the younger ridersBigham also pointed to how Red Bull's focus as one of the top teams when it comes to ITT research and development is mostly aimed at their up-and-coming generation of riders. With the best rider against the clock in the world among their ranks in Evenepoel, the potential trickle-down effect of his influence, Bigham's, and all of the Engineering team at the German WorldTour squad was visible in the top performances of Callum Thornley, who finished second on stage 18, and Finn Fisher-Black in sixth. "There's only so many tests that you can run over a year, and if you're going to pick anybody, you invest in that next generation that are coming through," explained Bigham. "Callum's obviously a great example of this, and Finn's had a lot of work as well. But also people like [Giulio] Pellizzari, like Luke Tuckwell, these are the guys who are going to be winning us races for the next five to 10 years. We want to invest early because this kind of stuff compounds. "It's not just that you find improvement and it's lost. You find improvement, and you keep building on that. You adapt, you get better, and you keep improving. And you've got to start that process early, when they're in the Devo team, which is a great thing for us. "We have under-19, under-23, and obviously World Tour teams. We have a great conveyor belt there. We have so many riders who are coming through and continue to come through. But it just means that my job ends up being working with the younger guys to make sure we put them in a good position. So when they get to the World Tour, it's fine-tuning and not drastic changes."In the end, drastic changes would not have changed much for Primož Roglič in his pursuit of red in the TT, but he was at peace with that, and with Red Bull admitting that Mas simply performed much better than any of their models could predict, they will simply have to live with that. Only an unpredictable miracle in the mountains from the four-time Vuelta winner can turn this race around now.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Knicks’ interest in veteran free-agent center emerges ahead of training camp
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: The New York Knicks have Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond positioned atop their center depth chart, but the defending champions remain without a traditional third center as training camp approaches and this saga doesn’t feel any closer to an end.In yet another update on the situation, according to SNY’s Ian Begley, veteran free agent Tony Bradley has emerged on the Knicks’ radar as New York continues evaluating potential additions for its remaining roster spots, with a competition for those expected to take place throughout camp and the preseason.“One other note on free agent signings ahead of training camp: veteran center Tony Bradley has also been a player on the Knicks’ radar,” Begley reported.If you’re like me, you probably though Bradley was 35 already. Turns out he’s only 28!Even then, and while Bradley would provide an experienced third option behind Towns and Drummond, don’t expect TB (or whoever ends up landing in New York) to find a clear and open path into coach Mike Brown’s established rotation.Begley noted that the Knicks are comfortable with their current top two options despite the absence of another traditional center, making it even tougher for Mystery Man to get any potential playing time.“The Knicks do not currently have a third center, but there is a strong degree of confidence internally in the Karl-Anthony Towns-Andre Drummond duo at the position,” Begley reported.Bradley spent last season with the Indiana Pacers and Atlanta Hawks, appearing in 41 games and averaging 4.0 points and 2.8 rebounds in 11 minutes per game.The 6-foot-10 center has eight seasons of NBA experience after entering the league as the No. 28 overall pick in the 2017 NBA Draft. Bradley owns career averages of 4.3 points and 3.8 rebounds in 234 regular-season appearances.Begley previously reported that New York has also shown interest in free agents Drew Eubanks and John Konchar while evaluating its remaining roster openings, hinting at the openness of the Knicks’ brass to land a variety of player types ahead of their title defense.For now, the Knicks’ next step is opening training camp before they face the Philadelphia 76ers in the first game of the preseason.

item.title: What's behind Alonso's cryptic comments about his F1 future?
Trump’s clash with Canada is his latest imperialistic embarrassment | Sidney Blumenthal
item.author: Sidney Blumenthal
item.content:encoded: The president’s chaotic schemes of aggrandizement, from Venezuela to Iran, have no larger rationaleTrumpism is the lowest stage of imperialism. “We’re not going to invade Greenland. We’re going to buy it,” Donald Trump reportedly told the annual black-tie dinner on 1 February of the private Alfalfa Club, an assemblage of prominent Washington figures, a number of whom he had publicly humiliated, and others he was investigating or suing. “It’s never been my intention to make Greenland the 51st state. I want to make Canada the 51st state. Greenland will be the 52nd state. Venezuela can be 53rd.” The room greeted several of his remarks with dead silence. His cosplay as the Pirate King was not received as a good-humored takeoff from a Gilbert and Sullivan opera. He went on. “So many people in the room I hate,” he said in a display of honesty. “Most of you I like,” he claimed. Then, at his peak euphoria, he flew off to Mar-a-Lago to plan his attack on Iran, which took place 27 days later.Trump’s imperialism of piracy and plunder is less of a system even than that of the earliest imperialism of 17th-century privateers raiding the Spanish Main, the divine right of kings, and monarchs dividing up the spoils as favors to create their lords and earls. His schemes of aggrandizement operating by threat and force are justified by no larger rationale, nothing as exalted as “the white man’s burden”, marauding wherever and however he can to seize resources.Continue reading...

item.title: Season over for Pauline Ferrand-Prévot
item.author: Patrick Fletcher
item.content:encoded: She has not raced since and, after reports that she would skip the World Championships, it's now clear that she will not race again this year. "In consultation with the team, it has been decided that Pauline will take the time to rest and recover for the remainder of the season," read a statement from the Visma-Lease a Bike team,"We wish Pauline all the best for the weeks ahead and look forward to seeing her racing with the team next season."After dominating the Tour last year, Ferrand-Prévot fell completely flat this time around, losing time in the time trial and in the punchy stages before the race even reached the critical summit finish at Mont Ventoux. By that point, she was down in 14th place, 14 minutes behind the leader, and the Bald Mountain would turn out to be the scene of her final pedal strokes in the race and in her season. Ferrand-Prévot had initially brushed aside any underlying issues, suggesting the level of the peloton had simply increased and even revealing she hit personal power records as she was getting dropped on stage 5. However, in announcing her exit from the race ahead of stage 8, the team stated that she "was not feeling well this morning", and Ferrand-Prévot stated: "I had to quit the race after being sick on the Friday night."It would now appear there's a bigger issue at play, with the team highlighting the need to "rest and recover" for the final months of the season. Ferrand-Prévot therefore ends her 2026 campaign, without a win, despite going close at the Tour of Flanders, where she was the runner-up, and Paris-Roubaix, where she was third as she and teammate Marianne Vos were outfoxed by Franziska Koch.She rode a fairly quiet Vuelta Femenina before turning to the Tour de France, where she was expected to lead the charge for yellow once again but where her season ultimately ended prematurely.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: As it happened: Stalemate among the GC favourites as win goes to the breakaway on stage 19 of the Vuelta a España
item.author: Stephen Puddicombe
item.content:encoded: For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go! Hello and welcome to stage 19 of the Vuelta a España! September 11, 2026 – 5:54 AMThere was a sense after yesterday’s time trial that Enric Mas had passed the all-important test at yesterday’s time trial, holding off the challenge by Primož Roglič in a discipline he excels less at with a healthy lead at the top of the classification still intactHowever, this race is far from over - and today’s parcours is prime territory for an ambush. As one of the few to exceed 200km , and with plenty of climbing along the way, including a summit finish, both he and his Movistar team must be alert, and again need to rise to the occasion. September 11, 2026 – 6:02 AMThe riders are in the neutralised zone, but one rider not among them is yesterday’s winner Stefan Küng. That victory made it mission accomplished at this Vuelta for the Swiss time trialist specialist, as well as delivering his Tudor team a second victory following Marco Brenner’s success - a fantastic return for one of the race’s smaller teams. September 11, 2026 – 6:11 AMAnd they're off! The first third of this flat stage is flat, so it could take a while for a break to form. The riders best brace themselves for a long battle.September 11, 2026 – 6:20 AMThe attacks are, as expected, coming thick and fast! For the time being we have a group of eight up the road by a few seconds but the situation is very much in flux.Here were the riders at the start, before hostilities began. September 11, 2026 – 6:30 AMHannes Wilksch and Mats Wenzel were the latest to try a move, but, along with a flurry of poursuivants, have all be swept up back into the peloton. The latter's Equipo Kern Pharma is especially eager for some success today, given the doubt surrounding their future as they continue to seek a new sponsor.September 11, 2026 – 6:37 AMThere have been plenty of attacks, but still nothing sticking, an 8-man group the latest to try to no avail. This looks set to go on for a while longer yet.September 11, 2026 – 6:44 AMPaul Double has abandoned the race. There's been no crash we're aware of, but the Brit has been struggling at this Vuelta, and was second-to-last at the bottom of the GC. Hard-going for a man whois primarily a climber. September 11, 2026 – 6:51 AM Jasha Sütterlin, stage winner Andreas Leknessund and soon-to-retire Steven Kruijswijk are the latest to try an attack. It's great to see the latter on the move and having some fun for himself, having done so much tireless work at the front of this Vuelta controlling the race for his Visma teammates Wout van Aert and Matthew Brennan. What a story it would be if he could take a stage win on the last Grand Tour of his career. September 11, 2026 – 6:57 AMAfter 40km of attacking, this trio of Leknessund, Kruijswijk and Sütterlin is the first to manage to stay out for some time and build a promising lead. They've got 25 seconds as things stand. September 11, 2026 – 7:04 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 11, 2026 – 7:10 AMLeknessund, Kruijswijk and Sütterlin are still leading, now 45 seconds up on the peloton. In between, some chasers are trying to join them. The fight is still on an the intensity remains high.September 11, 2026 – 7:17 AMThere is plenty of firepower in the chase group trying to join Leknessund, Kruijswijk and Sütterlin. Oliveira, Johannessen, Tronchon and Weiss have formed a quartet, and are now just 10 seconds behind, and 30 seconds ahead of the peloton, where things still haven't settled down. September 11, 2026 – 7:24 AMOliveira, Tronchon, and Johannessen (but not Weiess - he's dropped back) have now bridged up to Leknessund, Kruijswijk and Sütterlin, but the new front group are only a mere 20 seconds ahead of the peloton. It seems like there is enough in the peloton unhappy with the situation to not allow them to form the day's break. September 11, 2026 – 7:29 AMThe irrepressible Kevin Vermaerke is on the attack again. Aware that he's a superior climber, his UAE teammate Oliveira dropped back to pace him, and the duo have just joined the five leaders. Together, they're now 35 seconds ahead of the peloton. September 11, 2026 – 7:34 AMThis leading group of seven is working well together, and have built a lead of 47 - which must be the biggest gap any group has managed all day so far. The action is still very on in the peloton, where the attacks keep coming, and promises to continue to do so when they reach the day's first climb in just a few kilometres. September 11, 2026 – 7:41 AMThe riders are on the Puerto de las Abejas, the first of the day's three climbs. It's not the hardest of the day, averaging just 4.3%, but its length of 14.6km will ensure that climbers who want to get into the break have a chance.One such rider is Santiago Buitrago, who Pello Bilbao attempted to launch up the road, but he has managed to go clear of the peloton yet. As it stands, there are 30 seconds between them in the peloton and the seven leaders up the road. September 11, 2026 – 7:51 AMThe constant action at the front of the peloton as more riders try to escape to join the break on the climb is keeping the lead group (picture below, although it's now made up of seven riders, since Sütterlin was dropped) well within sight. They're just a few seconds ahead, and the battle to form the break is far from over. September 11, 2026 – 7:57 AMVimsa-Lease a Bike are hatching a plan for Sepp Kuss. Kruijswijk dropped back from the front group to help pace him up after attacking from the peloton. So far, though, he hasn't been able to join up to the leaders; nor has anyone else in the peloton, which remains 10 seconds behind the leaders as they climb the final 5km to the summit. September 11, 2026 – 8:06 AMA few riders have managed to join the leaders - Zana, Van Bekkum and Faura. Plus Eddie Dunbar, who bridged up earlier. While the break and the peloton remain so close on the road, the race is very much in flux.September 11, 2026 – 8:11 AMLeknessund led the lead group over the top of the climb, and since then they have been joined by a group of chasers. Briefly it looked as though Oscar Onley might be join, too, as he tried a cheeky attack, but the Brit (who is 5th on GC) did not manage to slip clear. As they descend, the leaders are 20 seconds ahead of the peloton).September 11, 2026 – 8:18 AMThis has been a truly relentless start to the stage, but there are signs, at last, that things might be about to calm down. For the first time all day, the peloton bunched up at the front, an indication that many are wanting to let the break go clear.But there are still some unhappy and wanting to join the leaders up the road, and another flurry of attacks begins. September 11, 2026 – 8:24 AMWe're almost halfway into the stage, and the race has just all come back together! Numerous riders had joined the lead group, to swell it to about 20 riders, but Netcompany Ineos paced at the front of the peloton to bring it back. The peloton is much smaller now as a result of how high the pace has been, but as things stand, there is no breakaway group. September 11, 2026 – 8:30 AMSo the action has re-set, and a new wave of attacks have come as riders try to form a new break. This has gone on for over 100km now - surely the longest battle to form a break at this Vuelta, and possible of the whole season. September 11, 2026 – 8:34 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 11, 2026 – 8:38 AMThe riders have been climbing the category two Puerto del Viento (the penultimate climb of the day; officially, at least), and Eddie Dunbar had managed to build a bit of a lead. He's being chased down by another group of hopefuls, among whom include the King of the Mountains Santiago Buitrago. September 11, 2026 – 8:43 AMDunbar continues to lead the race over the top of the climb, and so takes the KOM points. Behind follows a chase group of about 20 riders, about 15 seconds behind, including Buitrago.It's looking more promising for that group to join up to Dunbar and (finally) form the break of the day, as the peloton is about a minute adrift. But things still haven't settled, and more attacks come out of it as they near the summit. September 11, 2026 – 8:48 AMRichard Carapaz is at it again! The man in fourth-place on GC has used the descent of the climb to try and catch his rivals napping, and is part of small group that has a gap of a few seconds over the peloton. He's 5:17 down on Mas, but not the kind of man he can afford to give too much leeway to. September 11, 2026 – 8:53 AMYou sense EF have been hatching a plan all day, having been active at the front, and as one of the teams especially keen not to let the early breaks go clear. They've now succeeded in getting Carapaz up the road, but will be frustrated that their GC rivals are on the defensive - at the front of the peloton, Movistar are receiving help from Decathlon and Netcompany. September 11, 2026 – 8:57 AMDecathlon are doing the bulk of the chasing at the front of the peloton, rather than Mas’ Movistar, and have sent Sander De Pestel from the lead group to help the pace-setting.This is in defence of their leader Gall’s third place on GC, and it’s an undeniably defensive tactic - if they were being bolder, and intended to try to put Mas under pressure, they could have forced him to use up his Movistar teammates to bring Carapaz back, and then try to put the isolated red jersey under pressure with attacks.September 11, 2026 – 9:03 AMCarapaz's venture is over, as the peloton bring him back. His group managed to get a lead of about 30 seconds, but his GC rivals were not happy to let him build upon that.That means there's only one group now ahead of the peloton - a lead group of about 15 riders, about 1:30 ahead, and featuring Buitrago, and G Martin (who, in 13th, i the highest placed man on GC in it).September 11, 2026 – 9:11 AMThings have, at long last, settled down. Ever since bringing back the Carapaz chase group, the peloton has slowed down, allowing the lead group of 16 riders to build a lead of 2:30. We at last have a clear break of the day.The problem is, they don't have very long to build enough of a lead to hold off the chase from the peloton later on, with just 60km left to ride until arriving at the foot of the final climb. The break will have to work well to give themselves a chance of making it to the finish to contest for the stage win. September 11, 2026 – 9:19 AMIf this breakaway is to succeed, it will be the first stage since last Thursday will be won from a rider not representing either Visma-Lease a Bike or Tudor Pro Cycling, who have enjoyed a sweep of wins lately with their respective men Wout van Aert and Matthew Brennan, and Marco Brenner and Stefan Küng. Both teams failed to get anyone in the break today.September 11, 2026 – 9:26 AMBoth Pinarello and Groupama-FDJ (save for Tronchon’s stage win) have been quiet for most of this Vuelta, but are doing a great job today, having each got three riders into the breakaway. Also with multiple riders in it are Equipo Kern Pharma and Bahrain-Victorious with two each. September 11, 2026 – 9:32 AMMovistar have implemented the same plan that has served them so well since Enric Mas took the red jersey, putting Pablo Castrillo up the road as a satellite rider for later on. The remainder of their roster are setting the pace at the front of the peloton, with assistance from Onley’s Netompany Ineos team.Mas and Movistar again look firmly in control, after a very successful time trial yesterday. Mas is clearly feeling very confident, and not holding back talking about what great shape he’s in.September 11, 2026 – 9:39 AMNot fussed about the stage win, and instead focussed on defending the red jersey, Movistar are happy to set a light tempo and allow the break a big lead approaching five minutes. September 11, 2026 – 9:44 AMWhat will Felix Gall do today? He lost his 2nd place on GC to Primož Roglič on yesterday’s time trial, and was put on the defensive again earlier in the stage when the man directly behind him on GC, Richard Carapaz, went on the attack.We’re approaching his territory again, with a big summit finish at the end of this stage. With 1:24 to make up to take second place back from Roglič again ,we can expect him to make an attack.September 11, 2026 – 9:50 AMYesterday felt like Primož Roglič’s big chance to make a move on to challenge Enric Mas, but though he didn’t make the kind of inroads many expected of him, that does not mean his bid for the red jersey is over.Roglič has revealed that time trialling has not been a focus of his lately; which would imply that we shouldn’t read too much into his climbing form based on his time trialling form. He’s still got the ability, know-how and desire to put Mas under pressure on today’s final climb. September 11, 2026 – 9:56 AMThe riders have reached the bottom of the downhill they've been descending, and now must ride about 20km of valley road before arriving at the foot of the final climb of Peñas Blancas. The break's lead has been held at 4:45, which is a healthy one, but not enough to guarantee that the stage winner will come from one of them.September 11, 2026 – 10:01 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 11, 2026 – 10:08 AMThe break have done a great job on this valley section, and increased their lead to over 6 and a half minutes. It does now look as though they will survive to fight for the stage win. September 11, 2026 – 10:15 AMSo who from the break looks the most likely to win the stage?Guillaume Martin is the best-placed on GC, but could find himself prioritising making as many gains as possible rather than engaging in the tactical battle to win the stage - a situation he regularly finds himself in, having not taken a stage win yet in any of his many Grand Tour appearances.September 11, 2026 – 10:18 AMLeknessund certainly has the know-how, having taken a stage already earlier in the Vuelta; as does Eddie Dunbar, who claimed a couple at the Vuelta two years ago. The difficulty of the climb could suit him more than it does Leknessund.And as King of the Mountains, Buitrago is a prominent presence who ought to do well on such a finish, and is seeking a first Vuelta stage win having previously won twice at the Giro.September 11, 2026 – 10:24 AMThe riders are onto the final climb of the day! It officially climbs at 6.5% for 18.8km, but that average gradient takes into account some much gentler segments - there actual climb is far harder than those stats make it sound. It's long and enough and has sections that are steep enough to cause big time losses for anyone dropped early. This is set to be a thrilling fight for the stage win, and a dramatic one in the race for GC.September 11, 2026 – 10:28 AMThere's an early attack on the climb in the breakaway group, as Molard tries to get up the road; possibly as a satellite rider for Martin. He's dangling a few seconds ahead of the rest.In the peloton, it's Red Bull-Bora Hansgrohe who are leading on the lower slopes. They must have something planned for Primož Roglič.September 11, 2026 – 10:34 AMMolard has been brought back after his attack, and the break remains all together. That won't last, once the gradient kicks up and the climb starts to get serious. Meanwhile in the peloton, it's still Red Bull leading, showing impressive strength in numbers. September 11, 2026 – 10:37 AMAfter a long turn from his teammate Miguel, Buitrago has attacked from the breakaway group. So far only two riders have gone with him - Gloag, and, a few bike-lengths behind, Dunbar. September 11, 2026 – 10:42 AMRed Bull are trying to put him under pressure, but for now Mas remains comfortable in the peloton.Up ahead in the break, Berrade has joined the leading trio, while Castrillo is also trying to bridge up to them - he's clearly been given some freedom to ride for himself today. Movistar must be feeling confidant. September 11, 2026 – 10:46 AMRed Bull still lead the peloton with numerous riders, but the pace isn't especially high as reflected by the large number of riders still in the peloton.The break is also managing to hold a big lead over them, with an advantage now over seven minutes. If it wasn't already beyond doubt that they would contest the stage, it now surely is. September 11, 2026 – 10:51 AMA change in the peloton, as Movistar take over from Red Bull. They still have two teammates (Garcia Pierna and Romeo) to work for Mas, with Castrillo also up the road in reserve.Castrillo is also now losing ground to the leaders, and has been caught and passed by both Leknessund and Camprubí. His hopes of winning a stage are disappearing, so he may be called back by his team. September 11, 2026 – 10:57 AMStill no attacks from the peloton, but there is no a change at the front as EF take over. That suggests Carapaz is going to try something, having failed with an attack earlier.September 11, 2026 – 11:00 AMThere are still about 20 riders in the peloton, but not among them is Skjelmose, who has just been dropped. He's set to fall further down the GC, having dropped to eighth yesterday. September 11, 2026 – 11:05 AMAt the front, it's still the same four riders together - Buitrago, Gloag, Berrade and Dunbar. None of them have attacked each other yet, but will have to soon as the summit nears. September 11, 2026 – 11:06 AMMoments after that post, Buitrago attacked - and it's a deadly one! He's got a gap of ten seconds already, and looks very strong. Could this be the stage-winning move?September 11, 2026 – 11:09 AMDunbar is trying to chase Buitrago by himself, but still has ten seconds to make up as he goes under the flamme rouge.In the peloton, EF's Rodriguez has finished his long turn, but no attack has come yet from his teammate Carapaz.September 11, 2026 – 11:10 AMDunbar has closed in on Buitrago and caught him with less than 500m to ride...and now he goes straight past him! It looks like Dunbar is riding to victory. September 11, 2026 – 11:11 AMThe Irishman has done it, soloing the final few hundred metres to take the stage win. Buitrago comes home about 15 seconds later, with the consolation prize of a second-place finish and some more points in his KOM defence. September 11, 2026 – 11:12 AMAnd now Roglič makes his move! It's not an especially explosive one, though, and Mas, Onley, Gall and Carapaz can all follow him. September 11, 2026 – 11:14 AMOmrzel managed to claw his way back to the group, and the pace is slow enough for him to attack out of it. There's a stalemate in the group of favourites as they enter the final kilometre. September 11, 2026 – 11:16 AMMas takes control for the final metres of the climb to bring Omrzel back, and then Carapaz leads them over the finish line in the final sprint. Nothing separates the top GC favourites at the line, so it's as you were going into tomorrow's final mountain stage. September 11, 2026 – 11:18 AMThe winner today, Eddie Dunbar!September 11, 2026 – 11:28 AMHe was in defensive mode rather than aggressive today, but that was another day successfully navigated for Enric Mas. He didn't look under any pressure all day, and despite a lot of threats to attack in the GC group on the final climb, a move only came inside the final 2km from Primož Roglič, which he was able to answer. September 11, 2026 – 11:31 AMEdward Dunbar (Irl) Pinarello-Q36.5Santiago Buitrago (Col) Bahrain VictoriousThomas Gloag (GBr) Pinarello-Q36.5Urko Berrade Fernandez (Spa) Kern PharmaMarcel Camprubi Pijuan (Spa) Pinarello-Q36.5Andreas Leknessund (Nor) Uno-X MobilityGuillaume Martin Guyonnet (Fra) Groupama-FDJ UnitedChristopher Hamilton (Aus) Picnic PostNLKevin Vermaerke (USA) UAE Team Emirates XRGSergio Samitier (Spa) CofidisSeptember 11, 2026 – 11:34 AMPrimoz Roglic (Slo) Red Bull-Bora-HansgroheFélix Gall (Aut) Decathlon CMA CGMRichard Carapaz (Ecu) EF Education-EasyPostOscar Onley (GBr) Netcompany IneosJakob Omrzel (Slo) Bahrain VictoriousClément Berthet (Fra) Groupama-FDJ UnitedCristian Rodriguez (Spa) XDS AstanaMattias Skjelmose (Den) Lidl-TrekHarold Tejada (Col) XDS AstanaSeptember 11, 2026 – 11:41 AMAt the end of a long, epic stage of the Vuelta, which witnessed the longest battle to get into the break we've seen so far at the race, it was Eddie Dunbar who ultimately came out on top.The GC race didn't see much movement, with the top five coming home together, and just the one change in the GC as Skjelmose and Rodríguez swapped places. Have a read of our full report here.September 11, 2026 – 11:54 AMThanks for joining us today! Enric Mas managed to make it through today unscathed, but tomorrow could be another matter. It's the queen stage of the race, featuring a whopping 5,000m elevation gain across five mountains, including a huge summit finish to Collado del Alguacil.As brilliant as Mas has been so far throughout this Vuelta, this stage is potentially hard to break anyone. It's set to be a thriller, and could throw some real twists in the GC action; and, once again, we'll bring you all the action from start to finish on Cyclingnews.

item.title: The morning after winning the time trial, Stefan Küng pulls out of the Vuelta a España
item.author: Owen Rogers
item.content:encoded: Winner of the Vuelta a España’s stage 18 time trial, Stefan Küng has abandoned the race, reputedly to concentrate on the upcoming World Championships in Montréal.The Tudor Pro Cycling rider put in a blistering ride to win Thursday’s 32.1km individual time trial by almost three seconds, ahead of Briton Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), and is clearly keen to capitalise on the fine form which also brought him victory in the Tour de Pologne closing stage TT.With just 11 days until the Worlds TT, Küng will head to Canada to ensure he is in the best possible shape to take his first elite rainbow jersey. An accomplished Classics rider, Küng is primarly a specialist against the clock, and while he has multiple Swiss national titles to his name and is a double European champion, he has never won the individual time trial at Worlds, though he has been incredibly consistent.His best result came in 2022 in Wollongong, Australia, where he finished second, he was third in 2020 and has bagged a number of other top 10 finishes over the years."After completing 18 tough stages and winning yesterday's time trial at the Vuelta, both Stefan and the team have agreed that it is best for him to withdraw now," his Tudo Pro Cycling team said in a statement, according to Het Nieuwsblad. "Given the short turnaround between the end of the Vuelta and the time trial at the World Championships, and the exertion involved in international travel, this decision allows him to recover and fully prepare for the World Championships in Montréal, where he will compete in the individual time trial, the mixed relay, and the road race." While the World Championships time trial is 7km longer than Küng's victorious stage 18 Vuelta test, at 39.2km it is similar, especially with a relatively flat profile containing 200m of elevation. And on the form Küng has shown this summer, he will certainly start the race on September 20 as one of the favourites.This has not been an easy year for the 32-year-old Swiss rider. Joining the Tudor team at the start of the season, he crashed at Omloop Nieuwsblad, breaking his femur and spending a long period off the bike. He returned for the Swiss national championships in June, then took the stage win in Poland in August, though he only managed to take 12th place behind Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) in the Vuelta’s opening-day TT in Monaco.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: ‘Fresh from the roof’: the supermarket growing salad a few metres above the tills
item.author: Hannah Docter-Loeb
item.content:encoded: Customers seeking greens at one Berlin outlet are dealing with some very local supply chains indeedWalking into the Felix Thomas REWE supermarket in Lankwitz, Berlin, customers are immediately presented with a choice of greens: romaine, rocket, iceberg. But last month, a new option joined the selection: Lankwitz loose-leaf lettuce. A combination of head lettuce, romaine lettuce, Lollo Rosso, and dark green easy leaf lettuce, its yellow packaging makes it stand out in a row of green. But it’s not just the flashy packaging that makes it distinct. Unlike its neighbouring lettuces, which come from regional farms or all the way from Italy, these greens were grown just a few metres away – or rather, a few metres up. “Frisch Vom REWE Dach” or “Fresh from the REWE roof”, the bags read.Rooftop farms are nothing new: in cities such as Paris, Hong Kong, Copenhagen and New York, similar farms supply food to adjacent food retailers or even restaurants. This model has the potential to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from transportation (and its associated costs), minimise the urban heat effect, make use of dead space and perhaps even improve the relationship between buyers and their food.Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Just worry upon worry’: Europe faces a bleak winter as supply shock pushes factories to the brink
item.author: Alex Daniel and Lisa O’Carroll
item.content:encoded: From Shropshire to Hamburg, depleting reserves and spiralling costs are spawning a continent-wide energy crisisBridgnorth Aluminium has faced down Brexit, Covid and repeated energy shocks in recent years. But this winter is bringing extra “stress and pressure”, says its head of sales, Adrian Musgrave.Musgrave’s company makes rolled aluminium, used in packaging, construction and the manufacture of items such as cars and batteries. Like many stretched industrial businesses across Europe, Bridgnorth Aluminium faces a looming threat of soaring energy bills, which Musgrave describes as “just worry upon worry”.Continue reading...

item.title: Russell set to take F1 engine penalty after Mercedes introduces power unit upgrade
Is Isaac del Toro the new favourite for the World Championships? He says no but the road may say differently
item.author: Matilda Price
item.content:encoded: In a Pogačar free-world, where the level below him in the pyramid features many riders of a similar pedigree, assigning one rider that favourite status is not easy, but one name is top of the list for many analysts: Isaac del Toro.Teammate of the Slovenian and very much built in his image, including finishing third behind him at the Tour de France this year, it's not hard to see why Del Toro is an obvious choice to fill Pogačar's shoes in races like the World Championships and Il Lombardia, though the young Mexican himself isn't quite so sure.Despite his prodigious talents and swaggering confidence on the road, Del Toro is a different character when he speaks off the bike, and has never been one to over-egg his own chances, even now."No, I will say no," he said this week when asked if he could be considered one of the main favourites for the rainbow jersey. "Everybody is super strong. Everybody has their plans, and everybody has history in these kinds of races. As a nation we're still growing, and for sure I have the ambition to try to take the main spot, but yeah, it's hard."Del Toro is right that, riding for Mexico, he has to count on a smaller, weaker team, up against squads from France, Spain and Belgium, but at the same time, his performance at last year's World Championships seemed to dispel the idea that a smaller team could hold him back.In Kigali, he was the only rider who would follow Pogačar's eventually race-winning attack, and whilst he ultimately faded to finish seventh, he proved then that – big team or not – he is able to be amongst the best when it matters in the Worlds road race. After his success at the Tour earlier this summer – as well as victories at Tirreno-Adriatico, the Tour Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes and the Deutschland Tour – there's no reason to believe his ability will be any different in Montreal in two weeks' time."I prepare myself to be good, and if this puts me in the place to fight for it I will do it, but it's not a specific [training]," he said of his preparation for this block in Canada. "More or less my goal is to have the same shape all year and trying to do the best every race, and hoping for the best."Form-wise, everything points towards Del Toro being in a shape that certainly can compete with the best in the next few races, as he has been doing all year."I mean my level is not getting super high week by week, but I will say that I am more or less the same guy [that I was in] February, and hopefully I just can be more healthy and be good for these races that I have in the final part of the year," he said. "Let's see, if I have a good day, maybe I can be in the front."And if he can be in the front, it seems hard to imagine that Del Toro won't be able to chase after that rainbow jersey, or at least a first World Championships medal.Despite playing down his favourite status for the world title race in a few weeks' time, Del Toro couldn't help but let that confidence slip out when it comes to the races coming this weekend."Which race would be better to win, Montréal or Quebec? Which one would mean more to you?" a journalist asked.The answer was quick, and with a smile: "Both."And if he does win both, well, he won't be able to deny his Worlds favourite status much longer.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: 'You've got that pressure in your head' - Kern Pharma hit final days of Vuelta a España in last-ditch battle to continue in 2027
item.author: Alasdair Fotheringham
item.content:encoded: At a time when local fans are celebrating the renaissance of Enric Mas and the reemergence of Movistar as a major GC player, you might be forgiven for thinking that Spanish cycling is hitting a new high. However, not so far behind the scenes, things are not so looking nearly so rosy for the professional sport.A few months back when Kern Pharma, a Catalan pharmaceutical company, announced they were going to end their backing of their ProTeam at the end of 2026, there were high hopes that a new sponsor could be found in time for 2027. Instead, whilst conversations are ongoing on numerous fronts, nothing - yet - has been signed, and as things stand Kern Pharma, a team with a long and distinguished history both as ProTeam and before that as a top feeder amateur team, Lizarte, will be folding. Not only that, the future of Kern's own feeder team, Finisher, is also currently in doubt.Whilst team manager Juanjo Oroz has given riders and staff carte blanche to look for employment elsewhere, the former Euskaltel-Euskadi pro is still not throwing in the towel. Even the first round of application deadlines for Pro Teams for 2027 next week is not a definitive one, given squads only pay a small fine if they miss the initial date and then subsequently confirm they will be continuing.As for the riders, whilst there are rumours, according to Daniel Benson's Substack, that the former Vuelta a España stage winner Urko Berrade will be heading to EF Education-EasyPost, and some staff members have reportedly found new employment, a significant number are just crossing their fingers that they will still be in a job somewhere next year and hopefully at whatever Kern becomes."We're after winning a stage every day, and we're trying really hard and showing that we can," Iñigo Elósegui, a 28-year-old allrounder and former U23 Spanish National Champion racing the Vuelta for Kern Pharma, told ."But it's true that you've got that pressure and tension in your head about trying to keep the team going for 2027 and that right now we've got nothing for next year and we've got to do as well as we can for the squad. So it's difficult to race like that."I'm riding with that pressure, myself, that it could be my last race, and I have to do the best I can. It's been like that for the last few months and it's complicated."But the team atmosphere is good and we're working well together and that helps us keep our morale."Already in one 121 kilometre break through the ultra-hilly stage to Loja - which was how he won the Spanish 23-Nationals all those years ago - the Vuelta is also where Kern Pharma have delivered their standout performances as a collective too. Two years ago, the squad took no less than three stage wins, the most in the Vuelta for a wildcard team since 2012, and while the squad will continue to race both in the Tour de Langkawi and various Italian and French Classics before the end of the 2027 season, they know the next three days in the Vuelta are the biggest showcase they have left to impress a sponsor. In Elósegui's case, given he's not even sure where he's racing after Sunday, that's even more the case.It's often thought that when top teams and riders in a country are succeeding, as is the case with Enric Mas and the Vuelta a España, there's bound to be some kind of trickle-down benefit for cycling as a whole. But just as the 'trickle-down' theory of economics has been disproven time and again, that's also the case, regrettably in cycling, and Mas and Movistar's boom time does not mean their squad's former feeder team is also feeling the good news vibe."It's true there are a lot more public out on the roads and a lot more interest generally thanks to what's happening [with Mas leading the Vuelta], but the thing is, backing a cycling team costs a lot of money," Elósegui points out. "It can't just happen overnight just because it's a great time for Movistar, it's a long-term thing."Juanjo, our manager is working very hard on that front but it's very difficult to find a sponsor just like that."As for the 28-year-old himself, "I'm in good shape. I have a job which isn't so high profile because I'm there to help the teammates behind the scenes as a domestique, but fortunately I'm feeling really good. So I'm happy, and proud but even with good legs, in this kind of situation, it's complicated.""In the last week, there's not really been many opportunities for breakways, either. It's all high mountains or sprints. I've been working for [Marc] Brustenga, our sprinter as a leadout man, and then I'll try and help get our climbers in the moves in the mountains."Elósegui has always been very interested in Japanese culture and sport, and he doesn't rule out following the wheeltracks of pros like Rein Taaramae, the former Vuelta a España leader and double stage winner who headed to that country in 2025 to continue his career, in the Estonian's case racing with the Kinan Continental squad."I've always liked the country and the culture, and during the pandemic I decided to study Japanese and I travelled there, learning more and more about it. Apart from Keirin, I also follow the racing there in Japan. They've got a lot of good young riders- they're mostly very explosive because they mostly do circuit racing, so it's tricky for them adapting to the longer races in Europe."But I've thought of maybe trying my luck there, if nothing comes through here," Elósegui says."It's true that during the Vuelta, the days are so long we don't really have time for that, once we're through here, I'll see what I can do. But everybody I've talked to about it who's raced there has said they're very happy with it."That might, then, be a last-minute career solution for Elósegui, grandson of one of the top riders in Spain in the 1960s, José Antonio Momene, fourth overall in one Tour de France and winner of stages in the Giro d'Italia and Vuelta a España as well as the Dauphiné Libére - now the Tour Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes. But regardless of past glory, the clock is ticking on Kern's future, but Elósegui says there is no fixed date in the team for calling time on a new sponsor. "Talking to Juanjo, he says there's no specific date, but if the season ends and we still have nobody, I think it'll be complicated. And in my own case, if I haven't found anything by then, I'll have to call it quits on this and look for work in something else. I have to think in my own future, too."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: The ‘great grid upgrade’ is off track – ministers should spell out the risks for bills | Nils Pratley
item.author: Nils Pratley
item.content:encoded: National Audit Office calls for greater transparency on £70bn programme that is running over budget and behind scheduleIt’s an open secret in the energy industry that “the great grid upgrade” – the £70bn programme to rewire the nation’s electricity transmission network to enable clean power by 2030 – is running over budget and behind schedule, and may end up costing consumers and businesses more in their bills than advertised.How far behind? How much more? It is impossible to get straight answers from the bodies overseeing the massive spending programme, which may continue at an even greater scale into the 2030s. The Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (Desnz), its in-house body, the National Energy System Operator (Neso), and Ofgem, the supposedly independent regulator, publish acres of information on narrow matters, but none provides a clear big-picture assessment: how is the grid upgrade really going?Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.author: Guardian sport
item.content:encoded: Nicolas Jackson is ready to impress, Spurs are scrambled and the 199th Manchester derby takes place at Old TraffordWith 10 top-flight goal contributions between them across three games already this season, the Chelsea trio of Morgan Rogers, João Pedro and Cole Palmer are the early pace-setters for the Premier League’s most prolific, fluid and high-octane attacking unit. But on the occasion of his 100th Premier League appearance, a scruffier and more ungainly unit will be hoping to steal their thunder, as high-flying Hull try to register a top-flight win against Chelsea for the very first time. Yet to score this season but with a couple of near misses to his name, what Oli McBurnie has thus far lacked in goal contributions he has more than made up for with selfless graft and off-the-ball grunt work, making a total mockery of Steve Clarke’s decision not to include him in Scotland’s World Cup squad. The Hull striker ought to prove a real handful for a decidedly porous home defence, and a goal would be a fitting way to mark a century of Premier League appearances. Chelsea have not won any of their past four league matches against promoted opposition and, given Hull’s blistering start to the season, victory on Saturday seems anything but a foregone conclusion. item.title: Boy developed "toasted skin" condition from using a laptop every day
item.author: Beth Mole
item.content:encoded: Fears that modern electronic devices may harm children are nothing new. Gadgets with screens of any size have long been allegedly melting, rotting, and/or corrupting the brains of youths for decades. However, a medical case report published this week offers a new and alarming way our digital doodads may cause physical harm.In BMJ Case Reports, two UK doctors, Mara Znagoveanu and Edward Artley, report the case of a boy who came to an emergency department with alarming marks on his abdomen. The marks were described as being in a patch about 15 centimeters (6 inches) wide, made of flat, reddish-brown "interlacing lines forming irregular circles and a lace-like morphology." A picture of the marks is here.The boy, whom they described only as being in "mid-childhood," was not in any pain, and the rash was not warm to the touch or tender. He and his parents said they couldn't think of any recent injuries or trauma that might explain the marks. He was otherwise healthy, hadn't recently been ill, and had no systemic symptoms, such as fever or fatigue. Everything about the boy's health, growth, and medical history looked normal.

item.author: David Hytner at Old Trafford
item.content:encoded: It was a night for romance given the astonishing story that Sabah brought with them to Old Trafford for their Champions League debut. This is a club that did not even exist a decade ago and nobody saw their bolt to the title in Azerbaijan coming last season; in 2024-25, they had finished 41 points off the top. The job that their manager, Valdas Dambrauskas, has done since taking over in the summer of last year is extraordinary.It was also a night for cold, hard reality. Manchester United were back in Europe’s elite competition after a two-year hiatus and in need of something to soothe them after the trauma of their last-gasp coughing up of two points in last Sunday’s Premier League draw at Everton. And before the extremely serious business of the derby here against Manchester City on Sunday. They got it on the back of a first-half performance that burned slowly before catching fire.Continue reading...

item.title: LinkedIn beats "BrowserGate" lawsuits over scanning users' Chrome extensions
item.author: Jon Brodkin
item.content:encoded: LinkedIn beat two lawsuits over its practice of scanning users’ browser extensions, with a judge granting the Microsoft subsidiary's motion to dismiss the cases. The users who sued LinkedIn failed to adequately allege that they have standing to sue because neither asserted that they "had browser extensions installed that conveyed private information to LinkedIn," ruled Judge Vince Chhabria in US District Court for the Northern District of California.In his ruling on Tuesday, Chhabria gave the plaintiffs leave to amend their complaints but said he doubts they can make a plausible case. "Given LinkedIn’s further arguments that users voluntarily download browser extensions, which by their nature intentionally expose data to websites, it seems unlikely that the plaintiffs will ever be able to allege a privacy violation, much less prevail at the end of the day," Chhabria wrote.California residents Nicholas Farrell and Jeff Ganan separately filed class actions against LinkedIn in April, seeking to represent themselves and other LinkedIn users. Ganan's attorney, J.R. Howell, said he is evaluating whether to bring the claims in a California state court, which has different requirements on standing, or to appeal the US district court ruling in the US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit.
