item.content:encoded: While England makes its first foray into unfamiliar territory, it’s proved a boon for Italy’s cash-strapped municipalities A nightly tourist tax may be unfamiliar territory in the UK, but countries in continental Europe have been cashing in on these kinds of levies for decades.Tourists usually need to pay the tax on the day they check out of a hotel or holiday let, and are often surprised by an extra fee on top of their accommodation costs.Continue reading...

item.title: Demi Vollering set to lead a Dutch women’s 2026 UCI Road World Championship squad surprisingly lacking two former winners
item.author: Owen Rogers
item.content:encoded: Dutch national coach Laurens ten Dam has announced a strong group for the Elite Women’s road race at the UCI Road World Championships later this month, with Demi Vollering the team’s anointed leader riding both the road race and time trial.But the team is notable for the absence of two former winners. Three-time champion Marianne Vos and Anna van der Breggen, who won the road and time trial in 2020, were not selected. Vos has had a largely unremarkable season results-wise, the loss of her father severely affecting her spring campaign, leaving her with only one win so far this year. Earlier this week she announced she would be heading to Western Australia to attempt to reclaim the Gravel World title she won in Leuven in 2024, and it may be she feels she’s unable to be competitive in such a hilly race as the Montréal Worlds.The mystery omission is Anna van der Breggen. The 2018 and 2020 rainbow jersey returned from a period of retirement at the start of the 2024 season, riding to three victories since then. While she failed to finish the Tour de France Femmes last month, she won a stage and finished second overall at the Vuelta Femenina in May, before finishing third overall at the Giro d’Italia Women, winning the mountain time trial. The Dutch squad will certainly miss her abilities against the clock in the time trial on September 20.It was thought she would ride the Faun Tour Femmes, which started on Thursday, but her SD Worx-Protime squad started the French stage race with only five of the permitted six riders.After yet another brilliant season in which she won the Giro d’Italia Women and became the first woman to win the Tour de France Femmes twice, Demi Vollering was the obvious choice for the Dutch team.Though she’s come close, Vollering has never won a rainbow jersey, but with her uncanny ability to target races, she is certain to start the race as the out-and-out favourite. With 2,400m of vertical ascent over its punchy climbs, the 180km race on September 26 suits her down to the ground. Also riding both the time trial and the road race, Lieke Nooijen has recovered from a broken collarbone sustained in the recent Tour of Britain Women and proved her abilities against the clock by winning the national title in June.Should Vollering not be able to produce the rainbow-winning goods, Mischa Bredewold is another rider who could bring the jersey back to the Netherlands. Able to cope with the climbs, she has plenty of punch, though the same can be said for Puck Pieterse.Femke de Fries is another top climber, finishing third on Jebel Hafeet at the UAE Tour early in the year and producing a number of top climbing performances in the Tour de France Femmes, where she finished 12th overall."It is remarkable to see how many Dutch riders have made their mark at the highest level this season. I am proud to be the national coach of such a strong generation," Ten Dam said in a press release. "Demi is our leader, but at a World Championship, you need each other to succeed. The challenge lies in bringing all those individual qualities together as a team. If we capitalise on our opportunities at key moments, we can look forward to a great World Championship with confidence."Over the years, the strength of the Dutch women’s team has often proved to be their undoing, with so many top riders with big ambitions struggling to come together as a team, though if Vollering is as superior as she often is, there will be little opportunity for discord.Dutch women's team for the 2026 UCI World ChampionshipsFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. As it happened: time trial specialist wins stage while red jersey is successfully defended at stage 18 of the Vuelta a España
item.author: Stephen Puddicombe
item.content:encoded: For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go! Hello and welcome to stage 18 of the Vuelta a España.September 10, 2026 – 7:47 AMToday might just be the biggest day in the career of Enric Mas. A pro for ten years, the Spaniard has been one of the best climbers in the peloton for most of that time, but has never quite managed to deliver the big result that matches his talents. Now, with just four more stages left to complete, he’s on the verge of taking one of the biggest prizes there is in cycling (especially for a Spaniard) - the Vuelta a España. But to do so, he can’t just rely on his climbing, but will today need to call up on his more limited time trialling skills. September 10, 2026 – 7:55 AMThe man looking to depose Enric Mas from the top of the classification is Primož Roglič. While Mas has never won a race of this calibre before, Roglič has made a career of doing so; rather than hunting his first ever Vuelta title, he instead is looking to break the record for the most ever. As an elite time trialist, this is the day he has been waiting for to make a move on the red jersey, and will hope he can make Mas crack under the considerable pressure he is under.September 10, 2026 – 8:00 AMIt’s a flat course, and therefore one that should help the better time trialists among the GC contenders (ie, Roglič) maximise their time gain, while also giving the specialists further down the ranking a great shot at winning the stage. Have a read of our full preview here.September 10, 2026 – 8:05 AMMathias Sunekær Norsgaard will be the rider to get us underway in just a few minutes after which the riders will set off at one minute intervals, until we reach the top twenty on GC, from which point they’ll set off every two minutes; Enric Mas in the red jersey will be the last to start, at 16:55 local time.September 10, 2026 – 8:09 AMAnd they're off! Mathias Sunekær Norsgaard rolls off the start ramp to get this crucial, potentially race-defining time trial underway. September 10, 2026 – 8:17 AMOne of the favourites it also one of the first riders to set off - Ethan Hayter. The Brit was one of the protagonists of the first week of the race, starting with an agonising second-place finish behind Tadej Pogačar in the opening stage time trial. He's struggled since then, as evidenced by how far down he is on the GC, but if he's well-rested and feeling fresh for this time trial, he's one of the favourites for the stage. September 10, 2026 – 8:20 AMAnother contender for the stage has just begun, and it's another Brit - Callum Thornley. The 23-year-old was fourth in the opening stage, and as well as taking notes for teammate Primož Roglič, he'll also be going all in for himself to set the fastest possible time. September 10, 2026 – 8:27 AMToday's stage is held in El Puerto de Santa María, where the riders are setting off in turn from the town's bull ring. It's making for a spectacular backdrop.September 10, 2026 – 8:34 AMThornley has just gone through the first time check, and he's the quickest so far - 19 seconds quicker than his compatriot Hayter. They're both going for it, and are a long way up on the rest of the field. Theirs is the fight to be the early pace-setter, and so far Thornley is winning it. September 10, 2026 – 8:43 AMOscar Chamberlain, who was seventh on the opening stage time trial, is on the course, but is a little down at the first time check, 27 seconds slower than Thornley and 8 seconds slower than Hayter. Meanwhile Hayter is currently the quickest at the second time check - but Thornley is yet to pass through it. September 10, 2026 – 8:49 AMHayter has just arrived at the finish with a time of 35:54, having passed a few of the minute men who started before him.He's in the hot seat - but may not want to make himself too comfortable, as Thornley is still looking good to beat his time. At the second time check he retained his lead over Hayter, posting a time 23 seconds quicker. September 10, 2026 – 8:57 AMThornley maintains his pace all the way until the finish, and has put 29 seconds into Hayter. That could put him in the hot seat for sometime.That said, seasoned time trialist Ivo Oliveira is out on the course now and looking good, just 7 seconds down on Thornley at the first check. Watch this space. September 10, 2026 – 9:02 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 10, 2026 – 9:06 AMThe winner of both the previous two stages, Matthew Brennan, has started his ride. He won't be making it a hat-trick today, and will be taking it easier around the course, but whatever happens he's astounded with his performances at this Vuelta. His Visma-Lease a Bike has enjoyed great success in Grand Tours over the years, but this is their most prolific in history. September 10, 2026 – 9:14 AMIvo Oliveira has just posted the second fastest time at the finish, but he's a long way off Thornley's time, who was 27 seconds faster.The Scotsman's next threat looks set to come from Xabier Mikel Azparren, who has posted a time at the first check that's just 5 seconds slower. September 10, 2026 – 9:21 AMThere's just over an hour and a half to go until Enric Mas sets off for the most important time trial of his life. He's trying not to worry about how other people will ride, but focus instead on delivering the fastest time that he is capable of.September 10, 2026 – 9:24 AM João Almeida appears to have found some form! He's just become the first man to post a time quicker than Thornley at the first time check, albeit by just the two seconds. As a man who knows how to pace himself, you'd back him to go on to set the best time at the finish.September 10, 2026 – 9:29 AMRoglič might be the better time trialist than Mas, so much so that he has beaten him in all 22 of the stages they’ve competed in throughout their careers; but, looking back over all those previous results, Mas has reason to be optimistic. In none of those past stages has he lost as much as 2:10 to the Slovenian, which is all he needs to defend today in order to protect the red jersey. September 10, 2026 – 9:33 AMThat said, at 32.1km, this is a longer time trial than most of those 22. Here is how much time he’s lost in every previous time trial the two have competed in that were over 30km.2025 Tour de France: 1:38 (33km)2022 Vuelta a España: 1:04 (31km)2022 Dauphine: 1:11 (32km)2021 Vuelta a España: 2:04 (34km)2020 Vuelta a España: 1:43 (34km)2020 Tour de France: 0-49 (36.2km) September 10, 2026 – 9:38 AMBefore the GC race gets going, there’s a stage win to be won, and a couple of top favourites have just begun their rides - Bruno Armirail, and Stefan Küng. Both these riders have spent most of this Vuelta waiting for today, and have rolled off the ramp with the look of men on a mission. September 10, 2026 – 9:43 AMJoão Almeida has finished his ride - and he's narrowly slower than Thornley! Having been 2 seconds up at the first check, and on the same time at the second, the Portuguese slowed in relation to the leader and must settle for second at the clubhouse, 6 seconds down. September 10, 2026 – 9:52 AMStefan Küng is looking good, arriving at the first time check one second up on Thornley, though Armirail is further down, 10 seconds slower.Thornely is coming under pressure from all angles now. Having been 7 seconds down at the first check, Finn Fisher-Black is a mere 1 seconds off at the second; and another major candidate for the stage win, Wout van Aert, have just begun. September 10, 2026 – 9:58 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 10, 2026 – 10:02 AMFisher-Black has just finished, and he slowed down in the final third, fading to third place behind Almeida and his teammate Thornely.Still, that means there are two Red Bull riders in the top three, which bodes well for their team leader Primož Roglič. The word among them going into today's stage is that he believes he can win the red jersey.September 10, 2026 – 10:07 AMStefan Küng is absolutely flying! He's done a scintillating second third of the route, and is a whole ten seconds faster than Thornley. He's putting his all into it, to, and nearly overshot a corner. He'll be at the finish soon, so we'll know soon if he's going to maintain this speed...September 10, 2026 – 10:14 AMKüng has done it...just! He slowed a little in relation to Thornley in the final phase, but still had two seconds to spare once he got to the finish. Could the Swiss rider be on the brink of claiming the second Grand Tour stage of his career? So far things are looking good, as rival Van Aert is a substantial 8 seconds slower at the second check. September 10, 2026 – 10:22 AMWe're getting near to the GC riders. 20th on GC (and King of the Mountains) Santiago Buitrago has just started, and the riders have started setting off in two minute intervals. September 10, 2026 – 10:28 AMVan Aert is at the finish...and he's slower than Küng. He slowed down a lot towards the end, and must settle for fourth place.He was one of the few riders left who could realistically challenge the Swiss rider. Unless Roglič can better, he might be poised to take the stage win. September 10, 2026 – 10:33 AMIt's only been two years since Stefan Küng won a Vuelta time trial, his first at Grand Tour level after a career of frustrations and near misses. Could he be on the brink of adding a second?September 10, 2026 – 10:38 AMWe're now into the top ten, with Sepp Kuss starting his ride. This is where the riders have serious positions on GC that they will want to defend - no holding back from anyone from here on in.September 10, 2026 – 10:41 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 10, 2026 – 10:44 AMMattias Skjelmose has just started. As well as Roglič, he's the other member of the GC top ten who's an elite time trialist. He'll hope to move from his seventh place today, potentially as high as fifth if he has a really good day. September 10, 2026 – 10:47 AMOscar Onley is off. Carapaz’s fourth-place is a distant 1:20 ahead of him, so he might be looking over his shoulder instead at Jakob Omrzel in sixth, who is just 30 seconds behind and will also have his eye on the white jersey. September 10, 2026 – 10:52 AMHere we go then, Primož Roglič is off, to a big cheer from the crowd! He’s already won 15 stages at the Vuelta in his career, and may need to win another if he’s to gain the time he needs to depose Enric Mas at the top.September 10, 2026 – 10:54 AMThere is one rider starting in between Roglič and Mas: Felix Gall, who has historically struggled against the clock. The Austrian has just started his ride, and is expected to lose the slender four second lead he has over the former, but will want to ride as strong a time as possible to keep himself in with a shot of the red jersey going into the final climbing stages. September 10, 2026 – 10:55 AMAnd that’s it - now Mas starts, every rider is either on the road or already finished. Red always feels like a dangerous colour to wear on a bullring where this time trial route sets out from, and indeed he is a target today for Primož Roglič. But he looks calm on the ramp as he begins the most important time trial of his career.September 10, 2026 – 11:00 AMSkjelmose i through the first check, and he's not quite as quick as anticipated, setting the 22nd best time there. But he's still 10 seconds faster than Omrzel, so is in the running to take his 6th place on GC. September 10, 2026 – 11:04 AMOnley is going well, the quickest of the top ten so far at the first check, and the 14th quickest of anyone all day. His white jersey and 5th place are looking safe therefore, but he's still got a lot of ground to make up on Carapaz in 4th, who was just 10 seconds slower than him at the check.September 10, 2026 – 11:11 AMThe top three riders are through the first check, and Roglič is making gains - but not at the rate needed to take red! He’s put 21 seconds into Mas at the first split, and 22 into Gall. So far it’s looking OK for Mas, who is being roared along by fans on the roadside. September 10, 2026 – 11:16 AMAll the riders up to fourth overall have gone through the second time check. There's set to be no changes in the top ten as things stand, with Onley the quickest of all of them so far, building a lead over Omrzel and Skjelmose, but not enough to challenge Carapaz, who is limiting his losses to him to 21 seconds for now.September 10, 2026 – 11:19 AMRoglič is through the second check with the 6th fastest time of the day, almost a minute quicker than Gall. That's easily enough for the Slovenian to take second-place, but he isn't quite having the sublime day needed to really put Mas under pressure. September 10, 2026 – 11:21 AMMas is through the second time check...and he's 36 seconds slower than Roglič. At this rate he will still be wearing the red jersey on the podium tonight, and still with a decent buffer, too.Meanwhile Skjelmose has reached the finish, with the 22nd fastest time of the day. September 10, 2026 – 11:24 AMOnley has finished, and it's a very good time - the 11th best of the day so far, 1:15 slower than Küng. That'll see him extend his lead over Omrzel, and keep the white jersey on his shoulders. September 10, 2026 – 11:27 AMRoglič is giving it his all, coming out of the saddle sometimes to try to find extra reserves of strength to find what he needs to defeat Mas. But it doesn't appear likely to be enough - he arrives at the finish with the 4th fastest time, 19 seconds slower than Küng.September 10, 2026 – 11:31 AMGall finishes his ride, 1:47 down on Küng, meaning he loses his second place on GC to Roglič. It's not a bad time by his standards, though - only two seconds slower than Carapaz, in fact, so he'll remain in third place with a big buffer. September 10, 2026 – 11:33 AMEnric Mas finishes, to a mighty roar from his home fans. And he's lived up to the occasion! He finishes with the 12th best time of the day, losing little more than half a minute to Roglič. So he'll remain on top of the GC with a lead still in excess of 1:30. The Vuelta's is his to lose.September 10, 2026 – 11:36 AMAll that also means Stefan Küng has won the stage, a huge day in his career, in which he matches the biggest win of his career, from the Vuelta two years ago.September 10, 2026 – 11:43 AM1:37 is Mas' lead over Roglič as a result of this time trial, and an even healthier 3:01 over Gall, 5:17 over Carapaz and 6:03 over Onley. He'll still come under pressure in the upcoming mountain stages, and will need his Movistar team to protect him against attacks from those riders, but today confirms him as the clear favourite to the win the red jersey. September 10, 2026 – 11:52 AMA look at the results suggest that Felix Gall is the big loser of the day, as they only man in the top six on GC to fall down the rankings. But given that he was always expected to lose ground to Roglič, he might be relatively pleased with how he managed to limit his losses, and is still within striking distance of taking is second place back, if he climbs as well as he has been in the upcoming couple of mountain stages.September 10, 2026 – 11:57 AM“In the end, you have to win. It doesn’t matter by how big of a margin. Yes, okay, 24th victory, probably a few that I lost also by only two seconds or even less, so in the end, I’m just super happy to take the win here. I’m alone on the podium today, but it’s a victory for the whole team. And thanks to the guys also behind me working hard behind the scenes.“I think over the span of the 32 kilometres, you had to be dialed in from the start. When it’s such a fast time trial, you cannot have any costly mistakes, and when it’s so fast, it’s also hard to make a difference. I had a bit of a difficult moment after the second climb, but then I also misjudged a few corners there. But then I was able to get back into the rhythm, and so for me, that’s where I made the difference.”September 10, 2026 – 12:27 PMThanks for joining us today. Enric Mas looked more like a prospective leader than he has at any point so far at this Vuelta, and is now, having overcome his biggest challenge, on the cusp of sealing the red jersey.It's not over yet, though. There are a lot of quality riders behind him on GC, and, as a mixture of seasoned champions (Roglič), quality climbers (Gall) and irrepressible attackers (Carapaz), he is sure to come under attack in the upcoming mountain stages - starting with tomorrow. So be sure to tune in again for stage 19, where this thrilling race for the red jersey will continue.

A 'misunderstanding' leads US rider Evan Boyle to violate his own doping ban at the Dust Bowl 100 gravel race
item.author: Owen Rogers
item.content:encoded: Former promising professional cyclist Evan Boyle has been hit with an extra two-month period of ineligibility after breaching a suspension imposed last year by the US Anti-Doping Agency (USADA).However, after a tip-off that the 22-year-old had ridden the Dust Bowl 100 gravel event in Eminence, Indiana, on July 25, USADA has imposed an extra period of ineligibility on Boyle, extending his initial suspension from 16 to 18 months. While he has since been retroactively disqualified from Dust Bowl, his second place in the elite men’s 100 mile (161km) race is still showing on the event website, and a collaboration post on the event’s Instagram account is still showing.Boyle, who has accepted the additional two-month period of ineligibility, claimed he was not aware the Dust Bowl 100 is an event sanctioned by USA Cycling, which would bar the participation of any USADA-banned athlete. This defense was apparently accepted by USADA. "Following an investigation, USADA determined that Boyle participated in the event under the mistaken belief that his sanction did not prohibit his participation, as Boyle did not realize that the Dust Bowl 100 was a USA Cycling-sanctioned event," reads USADA's statement."Boyle’s misunderstanding was driven in part by the race materials’ and race website’s failure to mention that it was a USA Cycling-sanctioned event, although the event was listed on USA Cycling’s website."Nevertheless, the anti-doping authority still felt an extension to Boyle's ban was warranted, stating: "As with all sanctioned athletes, Boyle was responsible for understanding and complying with the terms of his sanction."Though he is not included on the UCI’s Registered Testing Pool, run by the International Testing Agency, Boyle is part of USADA’s Testing Pool and as such is required to provide whereabouts details, making himself available for out-of-competition testing. It was three breaches of this requirement, all occurring between July 16 and October 2, 2025, that resulted in his original suspension.On the road, Boyle spent two seasons racing with the Hagens-Berman-Jayco development team racing all over the World. While he won a stage of the UCI Nations Cup race, Tour de l’Abitibi in Canada, riding with the USA national team in 2022, his best results came at USA Nationals.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Thursday Posted & Toasted Notes: Underdog Knicks, turning point, forgotten Rose
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: Today’s post doesn’t merit an introduction. Just scroll down to the bottom, and you’ll find all you need.Jalen Brunson publicly pushed back on a rumor that he, Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges had reunited with former Villanova teammate Matt Kennedy by becoming clients of his wealth management practice.Miles McBride revealed when the Knicks realized they were championship material. He also praised former coach Tom Thibodeau for laying the groundwork, saying, “Thibs did a great job; he built a great foundation.”Mikal Bridges credited the Knicks’ postseason experience for fueling their remarkable comebacks throughout the title run.Josh Hart says the defending champion Knicks are embracing an underdog mentality (how surprising!) despite winning the NBA title.“I don’t think we have a big target. Because I don’t think anyone is picking us to win again. We’re using it as fuel. We’re still the hunters. We’re not satisfied with one. So we’re the hunters, and we like playing that game.”Derrick Rose says he never stopped believing the Knicks would win the championship. “I kind of had them winning the entire time,” Rose said. He also reflected on his own legacy, acknowledging he believes future generations may eventually forget him.Another former Knickerbocker, Danilo Gallinari, reflected on the biggest “what-if” of his career, saying injuries—not talent—kept him from reaching his full potential after being traded from New York in the Carmelo Anthony deal.Anthony Edwards again singled out Madison Square Garden as one of the NBA’s toughest road environments. Asked about his favorite arenas, Edwards listed MSG alongside TD Garden.Kenny Smith believes the NBA was justified in coming down hard on the Clippers over their salary-cap investigation, saying they were “vehemently cheating” and circumventing the cap.EuroLeague owners will hold a potentially historic meeting on Oct. 5 in Lake Como that could determine the future of European basketball, with club owners expected to discuss a possible NBA proposal to acquire EuroLeague following the league’s Board of Governors meeting. Yes, as we all knew from the get-go, the NBA doesn’t just want to expand to Europe—it wants to eat it whole.

item.title: 'Why not both?' – Remco Evenepoel kicks off 'Project Canada' with big ambitions and good feelings for Grands Prix de Québec and Montréal
item.author: Matilda Price
item.content:encoded: Tour de France runner up Remco Evenepoel (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) will return to racing for the first time since the Clásica San Sebastián this week, tackling the Grands Prix Cyclistes de Québec and Montréal as he chases some lofty goals in the final part of the season.'Project Canada', as he dubbed it on Strava, includes this week's two Grands Prix, followed by the World Championships in Montréal, where he'll seek to defend his world title in the time trial next weekend, and then add a second road race victory to his palmarès the following Sunday.Already the double Olympic champion in Paris two years ago, Evenepoel also has the unique chance of becoming the first male rider to win both elite world titles at a single Road Worlds.As a result, despite taking a solid break away from racing after the Tour, the work hasn't let up for Evenepoel this summer, who quickly returned to a long altitude training camp to prepare for the final goals of the season."The time went quickly. It's been a month without racing – after San Sebastián I had a few days of rest and then since then, I was training at altitude for three and a half weeks. And then the journey here, it was quite quick, so the last month has passed quickly," he said on Wednesday evening. "Everything has gone well. Training at altitude, it's always a bit different, a bit harder to manage the fatigue and training and everything, but it general it went well. There's still a little bit of time to get into the best form possible for the World Championships, there's still two weeks until that race. But obviously this weekend coming is going to be important for my preparation and finding my best legs, the best sensations, and be in the racing again."Though Evenepoel has a firm focus on the World Championships, where two rainbow jerseys are up for grabs, and admits that the first races are primarily about "getting the feeling back, seeing where I'm at", he's not a rider who can ever go into a race without at least half an eye on winning."Generally, it's preparation for the World Championships, but obviously there's the ambition to win," he said. "In every race, I'll aim as high as possible. That's how I start every race, so I won't approach these races any differently."Especially Québec, it has that very specific final climb. I think the climb suits me better now than before. That's why I'm here with ambitions to win – that's always the case when I start races. We'll see how it goes, but the ambition is definitely there to try and win one of the two, or why not both?"These are races that I've not won before, so of course I would like to add them to my palmarès. So I will start each with the idea of winning, that's for sure."And indeed, the other 'why not both?' question on the table is the matter of winning both the time trial and road race at the World Championships, a feat never achieved by an elite male rider in the same year."How often has a rider won both the time trial and the road race at the same World Championship? Never," he said. "That was my goal last year, and it is again this year. It is something I want to do in my career."Buoyed by his second place at the Tour de France, and indeed a fruitful Classics campaign before that, Evenepoel knows this is something he is capable of this year. The last few weeks of training, then, haven't been about reinventing the wheel, but more building on the form he already has, and shaping that around the final goals of 2026."I think it's clear that you need to have a bit more explosivity for these races coming, so obviously we've looked at that. We've worked more on the sprint. So the training has been a bit different to before the Tour de France. "That's normal because these aren't races where you climb for 20km, these races have more just hills than mountains, so it's different," he said."But in general I think we've done good work, we've kept the form I had and added some finishing touches, so overall everything has gone as we would have liked."The Pogačar question – and the Van Aert oneLike every big rider here in Québec, one of the main questions put to Evenepoel was about the absence of Tadej Pogačar, who won't be able to defend his world title after a nasty crash at the Vuelta a España ended his season prematurely. Without the imperious Slovenian on the start list, the expectation is that the Worlds road race, and indeed the GPs to come this week, will take on a very different shape."When Tadej is there, everyone wants to defend or just follow him, but it's not easy. I would say that now you have to come with new tactics. Clearly it's going to change [the racing] because normally you have to take control of the race. We'll talk about it again in two weeks, but obviously it changes things," Evenepoel said.He gently questioned Belgian national coach Serge Pauwels saying "it changes our whole strategy", and was understandably coy about what exactly that might mean."For me, in my head, it's not always best to say it like Serge did. It's better to keep the tactics to yourself a bit, but that's his choice. So yeah it will change things, but that's what it is, so we have to do it without Tadej now."What could also change things for Evenepoel is the fact that his compatriot Wout van Aert seems to be arriving at top shape just in time for the World Championships. Whilst there's debate over whether or not the course is too hard for riders like Van Aert, his success at the Vuelta has already started the debate around possible leadership struggles or divides in the Belgium camp.Evenepoel, for his part, was characteristically diplomatic when asked about that topic – as Van Aert has been too."I think he found good form at the right time. Obviously, it's still a long way to the road race, so he has to maintain it, but he has enough experience to manage the gap between the Vuelta and the World Championships road race," he said. "It's great to see that he's ready and in good shape. I hope he has a great final week and comes out of the Vuelta in peak condition."Whether that peak condition will be used to race for himself or to support Evenepoel, though, is another question, and one we probably won't know the answer to until the Sunday of the Worlds road race. item.author: Nick Ames
item.content:encoded: Valdas Dambrauskas takes Sabah to Manchester United after journeying from Lithuania and a game show win, via London pub work Valdas Dambrauskas can reel off the questions and answers without a moment’s pause. Who won the first Academy Award for best actor in 1929? It was Emil Jannings, even if someone else might have been tempted to go with Charlie Chaplin. Which country publishes the highest number of daily newspapers? India was the clear winner. Can you name the nation that produces the most electricity per capita in the world? His family, watching back home, clasped heads in hands but he was right: back then, in 2002, the answer was his native Lithuania.It was enough to win Dambrauskas about £725 in his appearance on Six Zeros – A Million, the Lithuanian version of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? “At that time it was quite big money,” he says. “I could have bought a flat in my home town; it was a very difficult period there and they were almost free. But my plan was to go to England and follow my dream to become a coach, and that’s how it started.”Continue reading...

item.title: 'It's almost my home race now' – Three-time winner Michael Matthews primed for return to revamped GP Québec at end of rollercoaster season
item.author: Matilda Price
item.content:encoded: As a three-time winner of the race, and many more times a podium finisher, Michael Matthews (Jayco AlUla) is always a favourite for the Grand Prix Cycliste de Québec, but this year the race will hold extra importance for the Australian.That's not just because the two Canadian Grands Prix this year are acting as a rehearsal for the upcoming Road World Championships in Montréal later this month – though that's of course a part of it – but also because for Matthews every race at full fitness this year feels like a success.He recovered in time for a packed summer of stage racing, being particularly active in the second half of the Tour de France, but this week in Canada will mark only his third and fourth one-day races post-accident."I'm feeling good. After the Tour I had a good block of training again at altitude. Then Plouay last weekend, I came straight from altitude, so it looks like everything is moving in a good way," he said of his form on Wednesday ahead of the weekend's races."Here, like every year, this has always been a big goal, coming to Canada and these races really suit me, so hopefully everything has gone to plan to this point."Coming back to a good level was not the biggest challenge for Matthews, who had already started 2026 well and with a win before his accident. That proved his base level and competitiveness is still very much there."Everything was going really well at the start until my big accident in March. Obviously that was a massive setback, because everything was going really smoothly after my health problems the year before. I was able to turn things around and get back into good shape after the in my lungs and then breaking both my arms and breaking my face was obviously a massive setback. "But I'm also happy to be alive. It was such a situation where if it happened again, I probably wouldn't be here right now, so I have to really be thankful for that and be thankful I can still be back here racing with the best guys in the world."This year, Matthews will face a revamped course in Québec and a route that's different from the one he's raced and won on before, so there is a slight sense of the unknown, and perhaps more chances for a repeat of last year, when Julian Alaphilippe (Tudor) won from a breakaway."Obviously where I've won the race three times suited me the best. Last year the breakaway managed to stay away, but I was still sprinting – if the break wasn't away, I was still sprinting for the win from the bunch, so it was OK. But now with the new finish, we don't know," he said."It's always different every year. This year is also very different when the World Championships is also here in Montréal, so there's going to be a lot of really good riders in top, top shape to perform, so I think it's going to be probably a different race to what we're used to, especially in Québec, but I'm looking forward to it."Matthews is so familiar with this city and these roads in Québec, plus there's clearly a renewed sense of confidence and happiness as the Jayco rider eyes a chance to break his own record of three wins in this race."It feels a little bit like I'm in Australia. I probably spend more time in Canada than I do in Australia these days, so I somewhat feel like it's almost my home race now," he said."Also I've had a lot of success here, so the fans obviously get behind me a lot, even when we're out training. Today and every day we're here, whether it's a car driving past or fans riding on the road, they know who we are, which is quite special I think. And these two races have brought cycling in Canada to a new level, which is really nice to be a part of."Facing big rivals, although not PogačarTaking win number four certainly won't be straightforward, though, particularly with the Worlds in Montréal meaning he's up against an even stronger field than normal, with potentially a smaller portion of sprinters and more climbing stars like Paul Seixas, Isaac del Toro and Remco Evenepoel.Matthews did get a sneak peak of the latter when they were both preparing for this final block of racing."We were in training camp at the same place in Livigno in Italy leading up to this, and I saw he was in really good shape, doing some really good training sessions," he said of Evenepoel."I know his focus is probably for the Worlds in a few weeks in Montréal, but I'm sure whenever he races he's going to try and win. He's a racer, whenever he puts his number on he's going for it. But Québec normally comes down to a sprint, but I think when you look at the start list this year, I'd say there's less sprinters and more climbers let's say. I think it's going to be a very selective race on Friday, I'd say."The question on everyone's lips this week in Canada is about how Tadej Pogačar's absence from the rest of the season might affect the races still to come. For Matthews, though, the Slovenian's nasty crash at the Vuelta a España was first and foremost a personal shock, rather than a racing headline. The pair are neighbours and close friends."I was watching the race from the massage table when I was doing Plouay, on the Saturday, so it was honestly very difficult to watch, especially when it's such a good mate. He was doing so well, he was in the form of his life, and about to create more things in history in cycling, so obviously to see that happen, ... seeing a friend really struggling, was super difficult," he said. "He was super helpful through my time this year when I had my broken arms, so obviously I'm trying to be there as much as I can for him during his hard times too."But aside from the personal element, Matthews – and all the other riders in the races this week, and in two weeks' time – still admits that Pogačar's absence from the World Championships, which he won the last two years, will surely reshape the race. "Obviously it changes a lot when you haven't got the world's best bike rider in the race. It does open the race up a lot more to a different style of racing. I think normally you would see probably a very hard race, and then a very open race from 80 to 100ks to go, whereas now I think people will probably wait a bit longer for the last few laps to start maybe a more traditional bike race for this year at the Worlds."Whether that's a race Matthews can be involved with is a bigger question, and it may well end up too difficult for his capabilities, but first he has a return to the GP de Québec to look forward to, a race he knows how to win better than anyone. item.title: 'You want to show why the team invested in you' – After crashes and stomach bug, gritty Oscar Onley looks to confirm GC top five and white jersey at Vuelta a España
item.author: James Moultrie
item.content:encoded: Oscar Onley's move to Netcompany Ineos has been far from simple, with the top GC talent being hit with several crashes and bouts of sickness ahead of, and during, the majority of his biggest goals. But his perseverance has seen him approach the final four stages of the Vuelta a España, with fifth overall and winning the Best Young Rider's jersey looking a likely possibility come the finale in Granada.The Scot made a flying start to his time on his home British side, competing with the likes of Paul Seixas, Juan Ayuso, and João Almeida at the Volta ao Algarve in February, but from thereon in, it seemed like setback after setback for the 23-year-old.In March, Illness forced him to pull out of Paris-Nice. A month later, a stomach bug saw him have to abandon the Tour de Romandie. A crash into a ravine at the Tour Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes in June – which could have been much worse – then ended his Tour de France hopes due to a dislocated shoulder. After the middle of those three DNFs, Onley took to his Instagram to vent an honest assessment of the expectations he placed on himself as a star signing for Ineos: "Been a tough start to the season to be honest and hard not to feel like I've let a lot of people down after all the time and investment from everyone at Ineos Grenadiers," he said.Having rebuilt to a position where he is now fifth in the Vuelta and four stages away from the second-best GC finish of his career in a GT, after his fourth place at last year's Tour, Onley feels he is finally back on track as hoped. "I mean I'm happy to be back at just the level to compete again," he told after stage 17 in Seville. "Obviously it wasn't the ideal start to the year or the start with the team, and when you join a new team you obviously want to perform and kind of show why the team have invested in you. So it's been nice to be able to get back to a decent level and be competing again."But this Vuelta, too, hasn't been without bumps in the road for Onley, getting hit with another stomach bug before the crucial climbing stage to Andorra, where he still performed well. He also came down in the crash that ruled then race leader Tadej Pogačar out of the Vuelta and the remainder of the 2026 season, before crashing again on a roundabout en route to Calar Alto, where he would drop away from the podium fight. Still, though, Onley has soldered on again in the GC race, and is now heading for the final three days which will decide the overall. He's still unsure of exactly how his body will react, but the confidence is there to cap off a solid performance in Spain. "I think I recovered well from my crash and a stomach bug in the first week, so I'm looking forward to it," said Onley. "It's hard to say how I'm going to feel, but in general I feel quite good just now."There isn't an obvious possibility of him improving on his current overall position, set to start tomorrow's 32km time trial to Jerez 1:20 behind Richard Carapaz in fourth, and 3:34 away from the final podium spot currently occupied by Primož Roglič.Onley could only admit that it wasn't his greatest strength as well, but he'll mostly be focused on defending his spot overall and lead in the BYR white jersey competition from stage 12 winner Jakob Omrzel in sixth, whom he will start with 30 seconds over on Thursday."I wouldn’t say I ever loved time trials, but that’s how I started cycling. It’s something I know quite well. I like the whole process of it; it’s just not my strongest area," said Onley after Wednesday's race. "I don’t know very much about tomorrow’s course. I will do a recon in the morning; I just know it’s quite flat and it will be a lot of time in the position. Any time trial causes gaps in the GC, and obviously, with 32 kilometres, I think there can be some big gaps between riders."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Vuelta a España 2026: Stage 18 time trial start times
item.author: laura@cyclingnews.com (Laura Weislo)
item.content:encoded: Enric Mas will tackle the biggest obstacle to his first overall victory in his home Grand Tour at the 2026 Vuelta a España on Thursday: the 32.1-kilometre stage 18 individual time trial from El Puerto de Santa María to Jerez de la Frontera.Mas doesn't have a great history when it comes to time trials in Grand Tours - in 2021, he lost over two minutes to Primož Roglič in a 33.8km test in the Vuelta. In 2022, it was 1:03 over 30.9km to Roglič (and 1:51 to Remco Evenepoel).The 2026 Vuelta a España, without Tadej Pogačar since he abandoned after crashing on stage 8, is a very different scenario and could probably be better compared to the 2018 Vuelta.Mas finished sixth in a 32km test on stage 16 that year, and hardly lost any time on any of his fellow GC contenders. In fact, he gained time on race leader Simon Yates and climbed up one spot after finishing sixth on the stage.This year, Roglič has been off his best because of an accident before the start of the race, and is third overall at 2:10. Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) is second at 2:06. With the rest more than four minutes behind, Mas really only needs to worry about the Slovenian.The stage will get underway at 2:07 p.m. local time with Mathias Norsgaard (Lidl-Trek) the first down the ramp.Of the early starters, keep an eye on Ethan Hayter (Soudal-QuickStep) - fifth down the ramp at 2:11 p.m. - as an early favourite for the hot seat.The most imposing figure in the time trial is Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike), who will be starting at 3:50 p.m. ahead of the wave of GC favourites.His teammate Sepp Kuss will lead off the top 10 of the Vuelta GC standings at 4:37 p.m., while Mas is the last rider to start at 4:55 p.m.The time trial will take an estimated 35 minutes to complete, so we will know where the GC contenders stand by 5:30 p.m.Be sure to tune into for our live coverage and expert analysis after the stage.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: NBA champion Dillon Jones signs camp deal with Philadelphia
item.author: Michael Zeno
item.content:encoded: The Knicks still have no idea what they’re doing with their open two-way spots, but at least for now, one of them will not be Dillon Jones, who signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the rival Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday.Jones has had quite the NBA career so far. He was briefly a Knick on draft night after being selected No. 25 overall in 2024, but his draft rights were traded immediately to Oklahoma City as part of a complicated night for Leon Rose and company.While he didn’t play much as a rookie, he won a ring as part of the 2024-25 Thunder. Most people coming off their rookie seasons on NBA champions would have some security, but Jones was part of the roster churn that OKC continually does to fit new draft picks on the roster, being salary dumped to Washington before being bought out of his rookie contract.Midway through the 2025-26 season, he inked a two-way deal with the Knicks, where he appeared in seven games and played 39 total minutes before being reduced to street clothes for the entire championship run. While you might think he was the least consequential of the 18, his experience as a champion was something Mike Brown leaned on as the reality grew closer and closer.The 24-year-old will now try to latch on in Philly, which has just one open roster and two-way spot with 20 confirmed players in training camp. He’ll be competing with the likes of Tacko Fall and Jameer Nelson Jr.If he does make the roster in some capacity, he will join Ariel Hukporti in receiving their championship rings on Ring Night on October 20 with the rest of the squad.

item.content:encoded: While much of the post-championship celebrations, the fanfare of the offseason, the roster moves, and their subsequent reactions have died down, one New York Knicks player and his future remain very much in flux. Deuce McBride, coming off a humbling Finals that saw him struggle offensively, has been involved in some trade rumors due to the uncertainty of his extension. But while fans and reporters have pondered potential trades and have lamented his postseason performance, some have forgotten just how good and valuable McBride has been. Gone are the days when every team’s best bench players are just prolific microwave scorers. McBride never has, and likely never will put up the kind of shot volume or record the sort of counting stats that garner traditional Sixth Man of the Year considerations. But the former West Virginia Mountaineer is a true “if you know, you know” ball player. In fact, he’s probably one of the more useful names in gauging an NBA fan’s knowledge of true winning basketball players and the non-star analytical darlings of the league. Yet, he wasn’t always like that. While McBride has become one of the more constant and stable rocks of this Knicks team, it wasn’t even that long ago that he was an afterthought on the bench. Stuck behind franchise star Jalen Brunson and fan favorite Immanuel Quickley, McBride began his career racking up DNPs and spending many a night putting on a Westchester Knicks jersey. Like so many players in the rotation, he strived to be in, though McBride never quit. He didn’t ask for a trade. He didn’t pout. Instead, he just worked tirelessly on his game. And the biggest example of just how far he’s come can be seen in his jump shot. While it was notably a major weakness of his early on in his career, the high release, high-arcing shot has now become a signature skill of his.Some of the credit also belongs to the front office. McBride put in the work, but the front office didn’t just stumble into the now backup guard by accident. They drafted him, believed in his development, and his presence was reportedly one of the reasons the Knicks felt comfortable parting ways with the aforementioned Quickley. It’s true that Quickley’s impending free agency and the Knicks’ reluctance to pay him were a big factor. As was the fact that the front office viewed OG Anunoby as the quintessential role player to put next to Brunson. But New York had the utmost confidence that they had a capable bench guard in McBride to fill in after Quickley’s departure. And that’s exactly what he did. Now, he isn’t the playmaker or scorer Quickley is. There’s a chance that McBride never gets there. But his much improved catch-and-shoot ability combined with his elite point-of-attack defense quickly turned him into an irreplaceable piece of the Knicks’ puzzle. He, much like Anunoby but in a much smaller package, was the kind of defender and shooter that could play with anyone in any system. A kin to the reserve guard he replaced, the fans quickly grew to adore him, resulting in the now-famous Deuuuuce chant that can be heard even in road arenas. What made McBride an anomaly, though, was the almost unthinkably team-friendly deal he was on. As the rest of the league and its analysts caught on, he became a mainstay on numerous lists. McBride’s name would show up on the most valuable contracts in the league and best bench players in the league list, amongst others, all while continuing to improve. He was starting some games, closing a lot of games, and regardless of where and when he played, the results were often positive. Very positive. So much that it became hard to find a Knicks lineup with a good net rating that didn’t have his name on it. McBride has had an interesting last couple of years, though. He was rumored to be one of the most vocal supporters of moving on from Tom Thibodeau- a very controversial decision at the time-although that hasn’t been fully confirmed. And he’s been relatively injury-prone during that time. Then there’s the aforementioned Finals performance where his shot had left him and his dribbling, or lack thereof, was put on full display against an incredibly physical and aggressive Spurs perimeter defense. Evaluating McBride on that series alone, and not the multiple seasons of excellent play, is unfair, especially when factoring in the injury he recently revealed he was still dealing with in that series. But all of that has put him and, quite frankly, the Knicks, in an interesting dilemma. The Knicks are clearly better with McBride on their roster than without him. And as of now, he remains one of the most impactful bench players in the league, who also happens to be on one of the best contracts in the league. Barring an unexpected extension, he’s going to hit free agency where the Knicks will likely lose him for nothing. But if New York’s priorities are to win another championship, they should risk that and ride out the year with him regardless of how flawed his offense can look against the elite defenses. But there’s also a possibility they try to prioritize finding another center mid-season by shipping out the backup guard. Regardless of what ends up happening though, it’ll be nice to start the season with McBride. And a fully healthy version of him at that. He’s a damn good player, and he’s now the longest-tenured Knick with Mitchell Robinson up north in Boston. It may very well be his last season in New York, so cherish it and celebrate just how far he’s come. Here’s to Deuce McBride. Happy 26th birthday, champ!

item.author: Niha Masih
item.content:encoded: India’s statistical system once commanded respect, and its data on economic and social indicators was considered rigorous – that appears to have erodedThere isn’t much that we Indians agree on these days. GDP numbers are no exception. Last week, India released glowing GDP numbers for the latest quarter – 7.8% growth – higher than the forecast 7%. It sparked a furore.Subhash Garg, a former finance secretary under Narendra Modi’s government and now a critic, reframed what Modi called a “herculean feat” as mere smoke and mirrors. According to Garg, the government revised last year’s current-price GDP downwards to inflate this year’s number – he believes the real growth is only 2.6%.Continue reading...

item.title: Nepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster
item.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Kathmandu
item.content:encoded: Foreign minister Shisir Khanal tells the Guardian the world’s biggest economies need to help Nepal, which contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions Nepal is demanding $20m in climate compensation for the recent devastating floods, as a senior minister called on the world’s most polluting countries to “wake up” and accept shared responsibility for a disaster that led to the death or disappearance of more than 6,000 people.Scientists believe the climate crisis had a role to play in the floods, which were triggered when a melting glacier partially collapsed and set off a deadly landslide and flash flooding through Chinese-controlled Tibet and Nepal in late August. So far, more than 1,300 are confirmed dead and more than 5,500 still missing, with hopes of their survival diminished after 12 days of rescue operations.Continue reading...

item.content:encoded: Mbeumo’s goal was a moment of individual inspiration but Michael Carrick will want more from Fernandes, Cunha and RashfordTunnel vision allowed Bryan Mbeumo seconds of focus, ignoring everyone in red around him, while those in blue provided a guard of honour. In a team game, it was an act of selfishness but sometimes they are the most satisfying, and Manchester United celebrated the single-mindedness when the ball rippled the inside of the netting.This is a new front four for United after Marcus Rashford spent last season at Barcelona but there should be greater familiarity between those who have already spent a year together. Bruno Fernandes is the instigator as a No 10 while Matheus Cunha, Mbeumo and Rashford try to create their own theories of chaos against defence through a complex potion of individual skill, tactical freedom and instinctive collaboration but the formula is yet to be perfected.Continue reading...

item.author: Andy Hunter at Hill Dickinson Stadium
item.content:encoded: Defiance serves David Moyes’s ­Everton well, especially when laced with a sense of indignation. At the end of a troubled week in the ­transfer market, and at the very end of a game when all seemed lost against ­Manchester United, they showed weaker in number need not translate to weaker in spirit.Ainsley Maitland-Niles, 19 ­minutes into his Everton debut, rescued a point for Moyes’s side with a stunning 25‑yard strike into Senne Lammens’s top ­corner with virtually the final kick of a game that slow-burned into an eruption. Benjamin Sesko had appeared to have delivered victory for United at Hill Dickinson Stadium for the second season in succession, with an 88th‑minute header past Jordan Pickford, but the visitors could not hold out.Continue reading...

item.title: The worst trades in Knicks history
item.author: Michael Zeno
item.content:encoded: The year-long probe surrounding alleged salary cap manipulation ended on Wednesday and handed down one of the biggest punishments in professional sports history, suspending multiple key officials, fining the organization $30 million, and taking five first-round picks. It’s not entirely unprecedented (see: Joe Smith), but it’s pretty damn startling.While there are many things to take away from this ruling (particularly with how Kawhi seems to have completely gotten away with this), the biggest thing might just be how unimaginably bad the Kawhi Leonard era went in LA.To get Leonard to sign with them in 2019, the Clippers had to trade for Paul George, a trade that has gone down as one of the worst in league history due to the sheer magnitude of picks traded and how it kickstarted the Thunder’s contention window by giving them Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.In seven years, it was disappointment after disappointment, with the highlight being a trip to the 2021 Western Conference Finals that ended in a blowout defeat at home in Game 6. George left and was replaced by James Harden; Harden left, and Leonard is choosing to return to Toronto after burning this franchise to the ground behind him.In total, with Leonard (likely) going to the Raptors at some point, this is what the Clippers gave up for his services, both to convince him to sign and convince him to stay:2021 MIA 1st (#18 – Tre Mann)2022 LAC 1st (#12 – Jalen Williams)2023 1st Pick Swap (not conveyed)2024 LAC 1st (#26 – Dillon Jones)2025 MIA 1st (Lottery Protected, became Thomas Sorber)2025 1st Pick Swap (Conveyed, Nique Clifford)2026 LAC 1st (#12 – Aday Mara)2029 IND 1st (voided by NBA)2030 LAC 1st (voided by NBA)2031 LAC 1st (voided by NBA)2032 LAC 1st (voided by NBA)2033 LAC 1st (voided by NBA)This is, hands down, the worst trade in NBA history. It destroyed an entire franchise’s future 10-15 years for three playoff series victories in seven years. At least Billy King only messed up the Nets for five years.It does get you thinking, though. How bad has it gotten for the Knicks? We can recall some pretty nasty trades from recent or even less recent history, but just how close do they get to the utter franchise-alteringly bad level as the Paul George trade?Gene Shue To Fort Wayne (April 1956)Ron SobieGene ShueWe’re starting old school, back when the Pistons were still based in Fort Wayne. Before researching this, I had no clue who these guys were and would be very surprised if we had anyone in our community who’s been around long enough to remember watching them play (prove me wrong if so!)Shue, the No. 3 overall pick in 1954, was sold to the Knicks just six games into his rookie year, but was nothing more than a regular role player in his near-two years in New York, averaging 9.2 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 2.5 assists in 1955-56.Very shortly after the season, the 6’2” guard was dealt on draft night to Fort Wayne for Ron Sobie, the No. 7 overall pick. Sobie didn’t do much in four years, playing 191 total games and averaging 8.5 points and 4.1 rebounds before being sold to Minneapolis in December 1959, where he’d play just one more game ever.As for Shue? He grew into his own as the Pistons moved to Detroit, being named to his first All-Star team in 1958 before getting down-ballot MVP votes over the next several seasons. He eventually grew into a 23-PPG scorer and made First-Team All-NBA in 1960. Five All-Star teams, two top-10 MVP finishes, and two All-NBA selections in six years in Detroit.The Knicks would actually get a chance to rectify their mistake with Shue, re-acquiring him for Darrall Imhoff before the 1962-63 season, but he started to regress in his age-31 season, and he was out of basketball by the end of 1964.While Shue never won Detroit a championship, he would’ve been a tremendous help to a Knicks team that went through its first Dark Ages prior to the 70s revival. In the six years with Shue in Detroit, the Knicks had one losing season and won sub-30 games in three of those seasons. Choosing $4.8 Million Over Julius Erving (1976)This is, unequivocally, the worst decision in franchise history. All of these other moves were trades that went wrong, but in the spirit of bad decisions, we’re going to cover this as well.When the Nets were among the teams chosen to join the NBA after the ABA merger in 1976, the Knicks demanded that they pay a fee of $4.8 million (over 10 years) for encroaching on their territorial rights, a request that was sustained by the NBA alongside their $3.2 million fee for joining the league. In total, the Nets had to come up with $8 million just to exist.The Knicks would get their money, alongside eventually suing the Nets and forcing them to move from Long Island to New Jersey, but made an unforgivable, disgusting error in the process.Dr. J made $350,000 during this time, but wanted a renegotiation. As such, the Nets were willing to offload his salary and offered him to the Knicks, then owned by the Graham Paige Corporation and ran by Eddie Donovan in the front office.The Knicks said no. They chose a few million, which was a lot at the time to be fair, over a future Hall of Famer.Philadelphia purchased Erving for $3 million, and the rest is history. The Knicks let a rival get the best incoming ABA talent available and watched him lead the Sixers to a championship in 1983 while spending over a decade as a top-five player in the game.Oh yeah, not to mention that the Knicks were mostly irrelevant during his time in the league and got swept twice by the Sixers in 1978 and 1983. Imagine if the Knicks could’ve gone from Clyde and Willis Reed to Dr. J. Ugh.Maurice Lucas to the Suns (July 1982) Truck Robinson Maurice LucasIn the time between the Knicks’ eras of relevance in the 70s and 90s, it wasn’t anything too bad in the 80s, just inconsistency as they waited for the next big thing in Patrick Ewing to get them back into contention.They seemed to stumble upon something huge in the summer of 1981, when the New Jersey Nets sent them a 28-year-old Maurice Lucas as a form of compensation for signing Ray Williams in free agency. Think of it as a precursor to a sign-and-trade. Nonetheless, the team got a former All-Star and All-Defense power forward still in his athletic prime.In his one year in New York, Lucas averaged 15.8 points and 11.3 rebounds while shooting 50.3% from the field. It was his best overall season since he was in Portland, but the Knicks never saw him a long-term option, shipping him to Phoenix for Truck Robinson one year later.The deal made sense at the time, as Robinson was even more productive than Lucas the season prior, but he hit hard regression in his age-31 season in 1982-83 and only lasted two seasons in New York, flaming out by age 33. He would hear it from the fans, being nicknamed “Dump Truck” for his startling fall-off.Meanwhile, Lucas made his fifth All-Star team in his first year in Phoenix as part of a second prime that slowly dissipated a few years later. While Lucas would only have 2-3 years of All-Star level talent post-trade, it was a helluva lot better than Robinson.They could’ve used that force at PF, you know. Bernard King and Bill Cartwright carried the Knicks to consecutive playoff appearances in 1983 and 1984, with the latter team being a game away from the Eastern Conference Finals. Just imagine how it would go if Lucas were there instead of Robinson.Then again, if not for the dismantling of that team following the 1983-84 season, Ewing might not have ever been a Knick. Food for thought. Rod Strickland To San Antonio (February 1990) Maurice CheeksRod StricklandThe Knicks had their reasons for making this trade, it just aged badly.Strickland was a solid backup point guard in his first year and a half in the league, but was blocked by Mark Jackson. The Knicks, who had risen to become a perennial playoff team in the late 80s, were thinking about getting to the next level, so they traded a young guard who was blocked for a 33-year-old veteran who could fit the role better as one of the league’s best defensive guards.Cheeks, an NBA champion in Philly in 1983 and again as an assistant on this year’s staff, played a total of 107 games as a Knick, averaging eight points and five assists while adequately raising his game in the postseason. He was shipped out prior to 1991-92 for a pick that became Charlie Ward before retiring a year later. The player they got was fine, but they definitely could’ve used Strickland.Jackson had a ceiling as a Knick, one that he reached quite early and led to his departure after 1991-92. Strickland, meanwhile, would become a great starting guard in San Antonio and Portland, eventually averaging 19 points and nine assists in his prime during the mid-to-late 90s.I wonder if an offensively challenged Knicks team, one that relied on gritty defense without a true point guard and having to rely on John Starks (more of a 2-guard) to provide playmaking. Imagine if Strickland was the point guard instead of Doc Rivers in 1994.The Eddy Curry Fiasco (October 2005)Eddy Curry, Antonio DavisJermaine Jackson, Mike Sweetney, Tim Thomas, 2006 NYK 1st, 2007 Pick Swap, 2007 NYK 2nd, 2009 NYK 2ndIsiah Thomas is damn lucky I’m only including one of his trades.This was really bad. Eddy Curry was a fine player for the Bulls, one who was worth a decent salary and averaged 16 points and five rebounds at the end of his rookie contract. Putting aside the fact that he was seven-foot and grabbed way less rebounds than an average center, it’s a fine guy to trade for.But that much? In a sign-and-trade? And you give him $60 million over six years to make the 23-year-old the sixth-highest-paid center in basketball? After seeing the Bulls drag their feet on an extension because of an irregular heartbeat? Seriously?The players they gave up weren’t a big deal. Jermaine Jackson never played for the Bulls. Mike Sweetney replaced Curry as the starting center and was much worse before being out of the league by 2008. Tim Thomas played just three games as a Bull before being cut. It’s the picks. It’s the hubris of believing the team was an Eddy Curry away from turning things around.When Leon Rose traded a mountain of picks for Mikal Bridges, he understood that it might not result in a championship and assumed risk down the road, but also knew it wouldn’t immediately blow up due to the team having a very high floor as constructed. Worst-case scenario, the Nets get good picks in 2029 and 2031, not 2025 or 2027.The Knicks won just 33 games the year before. They added Curry, Jerome James, Nate Robinson, and rookies Channing Frye and David Lee, and hired the man who won a title with a Pistons team that was better than the sum of its parts two years prior. They made a gamble that it would all work.It didn’t. At all. They won just 23 games despite James Dolan paying luxury tax. They had the second-worst record in basketball, and they’d get nothing for it. The Bulls got the No. 2 pick in the draft and had future All-Star LaMarcus Aldridge fall into their lap. Now, they messed that up by sending him to Portland for Tyrus Thomas and Viktor Khryapa, but the point remains.The following year, the Knicks won just 33 games after Isiah took over as head coach. The Bulls won a bunch more, exercising the swap and taking the No. 9 pick, which became future Defensive Player of the Year Joakim Noah.The two top picks traded for Curry became two of the best big men of their generation. The second picks didn’t result in much, but the Bulls traded the 2007 2nd for Thabo Sefolosha and the 2009 2nd in a weird future swap with Portland, but the damage remains.As for Curry on the Knicks, he had a great 2006-07, averaging 19.5 points and seven rebounds. After that, with four years left on his contract, he played a total of 69 more games as a Knick as he battled injuries, his weight, and a bad work ethic. Complete, franchise-altering disaster.Tracy McGrady Becomes a Knick (February 2010)Tracy McGrady, Sergio RodriguezJordan Hill, Jared Jeffries, Hilton Armstrong, Kevin Martin, 2011 Pick Swap, 2012 NYK 1st Joey Dorsey, Carl Landry, Larry HughesThis trade wasn’t catastrophic by any means, but it’s inclusion is meant to represent all the times over the years that management traded draft picks for absolutely no reason, headlined by its most baffling.A first-round pick, a swap, the guy you picked in the lottery literally eight months ago, and Jared Jeffries… for a 31-year-old rental who’s past his prime. It embodies the incompetence of the Knicks back then.Jordan Hill wasn’t good, but they picked him between Steph Curry and DeMar DeRozan in June 2009. It’s ridiculous to give up on this guy that quickly, and it says a lot about the front office’s drafting ability and thought process. Jeffries and Hughes were okay role players. None of these guys would come back to bite you.But like the Curry trade, it’s the damn picks. The 2011 swap didn’t convey because, unlike Isiah, Donnie Walsh actually added good players in between to ensure no collapse, as Amar’e Stoudemire lifted the Knicks to the postseason in 2011 (disregard that Houston had a better record and the West being a gauntlet was the only reason the swap didn’t convey). The 2012 pick landed at No. 16, but the 2012 draft was hilariously shallow, so Royce White doesn’t come back to bite him.As for McGrady and Rodriguez? Neither of them played for the Knicks past April 2010. McGrady, particularly, played abysmally in 24 starts down the stretch and had to settle for a veteran minimum with the Pistons that summer. For a team that, at the time of the trade, was well below .500, it’s completely inconceivable.Well, I guess it was meant to open up cap space for LeBron and company that offseason, and while Amar’e was a solid consolation prize (for a minute), the franchise’s incompetence at that point made it rather foolish to think the best player in the world was dying to come there. Good thing we didn’t do this again nine years later!Acquiring Carmelo Anthony (February 2011)Carmelo Anthony, Renaldo Balkman, Chauncey Billups, Anthony Carter, Shelden Williams, Corey BrewerWilson Chandler, Raymond Felton, Danilo Gallinari, Timofey Mozgov, Kosta Koufos, 2014 NYK 1st, 2016 Pick Swap, 2012 GSW 2nd, 2013 NYK 2ndEddy Curry, Anthony Randolph, 2015 DEN 2ndHere’s a bold one, and no, I’m not saying this as someone who doesn’t like Melo. He was my favorite Knick when I first got into this team and I’ll always have a soft spot for him. The trade itself is relatively fine; the problem lies with the circumstances surrounding it.Melo was due to be an unrestricted free agent that summer. The Knicks had plenty of space to give him the new max contract he desired from Denver. Instead of waiting until the summer to pair him with Amar’e in a move many believed was obvious, a paranoid Donnie Walsh was terrified of the crosstown Nets getting him instead, with the whole “Jay-Z as part-owner” schtick. Melo was not choosing the damn Nets, but the Knicks weren’t taking that risk.It was a huge, 13-player trade, one that also involved dumping Curry’s contract to Minnesota. Let’s break down the guys that came with Melo, who’s story in New York is well known already:Renaldo Balkman, who was drafted by the Knicks and traded to Denver in July 2008, played just 17 games after this trade in the next two seasons.34-year-old Chauncey Billups actually played very well in 21 starts down the stretch as an expiring contract, which convinced the Clippers he still had it (he played just 42 games in the next two seasons). Anthony Carter played 19 games as a Knick before signing with the Raptors that offseason. He played his last game in 2011-12. Shelden Williams played 17 games (started six) down the stretch. The big man ended his career with New Jersey the following season, playing just 58 more games.Corey Brewer spent six days on the roster before being waived. He won a ring in Dallas that year, and his best years were ahead of him. Whoops.As for what they gave up? Felton would eventually return a few years later, but the other three had solid NBA careers where they made a lot of money (looking at you, Mozgov). Gallinari’s marksmanship and Chandler’s solid play as a bench wing could’ve been useful off the bench during the Knickstape era, but they were just so horrified of Jay-Z.The real kicker is the picks, again. Not that they were too damaging, just how funny it wound up being:2012 GSW 2nd: Landed No. 38, turned into Quincy Miller. Unrelated, Khris Middleton went one pick later. Good job, Nuggies.2013 GSW 2nd: Landed No. 51 and was traded to Orlando in the complicated Dwight Howard trade. Became Romero Osby, who never played in the NBA. Did I mention they got these two seconds for trading away David Lee?2014 NYK 1st: Landed No. 12 after a shockingly bad 2013-14 season, but was also sent to Orlando in Dwight trade. Became Dario Saric, who was then sent to PhillyThen there’s the 2016 pick swap. Both Denver and New York stunk in 2015-16, but the Knicks did lose one more game, landing them the No. 7 pick, which would then go to Denver. That became All-Star guard Jamal Murray.I got good news and bad news from here.Good news: by virtue of the swap, the Knicks landed the No. 9 pick in the draft, so the swap wasn’t that bad!Bad news: because of the next trade, they didn’t make that selection.The Andrea Bargnani Trade (July 2013)Andrea BargnaniMarcus Camby, Steve Novak, Quentin Richardson, 2016 Swap Worst w/DEN, 2014 OKC 2nd, 2017 NYK 2ndVibes were high in the Summer of ‘13. After all, the Knicks had gotten to the second round of the playoffs for the first time in 13 years. Sure, it was a disappointing exit at the hands of the Pacers, but they felt as if their core still had some mileage in it with Melo, Amar’e, Tyson Chandler, Mike Woodson, and friends.Let’s add another chef to the mix. Enter Bargnani, a failure of a No. 1 pick who enjoyed some solid seasons as Chris Bosh’s second fiddle before becoming a 20-PPG scorer in 2010-11. The two seasons before the trade, he was limited to 65 games, while his stretch-four abilities waned and his three-point shooting regressed sharply. An elbow injury suffered the year before the trade seemed not to dissuade management. The players they gave up were more sentimental than skilled. Camby was a remnant of the transition from Ewing to Houston/Sprewell, having rejoined the Knicks that past season for the final 24 games of his career at age-38. Richardson was effectively the same, having played one game in 2012-13 in his second stint as a Knick after a nice, four-year run in the 2000s before retiring. Discount Double Check was a fan-favorite sniper, but one that was moved on from at the right time as his minutes and production completely cratered post-trade.Once again, it’s the picks.The OKC 2nd landed at No. 59 and was worthless. The 2017 pick landed at No. 36, which was eventually sent to Philly and became Jordan Bolden. Good thing this wasn’t a 2018 pick, phew. The real problem was a swapThe Knicks elected to make a rare move, trading the back end of a pick swap they had already traded. Essentially, Toronto got the worst of their picks and Denver’s picks. The odds of that being in the lottery were slim, but it handed Jakob Poeltl, a solid NBA big man for the last decade, right to them at No. 9. As for Bargnani’s Knicks career, he sucked. He was the poster child of the team’s failure to maximize the rest of Melo’s prime, as Amar’e regressed hard, Chandler was traded, and this guy made eight figures to make boneheaded decision after boneheaded decision while battling injury. He played just 71 games as a Knick, made $23 million, and was dumped out the door after 2014-15. What a waste.
